# Hermes Agent - Development Guide

Instructions for AI coding assistants and developers working on the hermes-agent codebase.
This root file holds only what applies everywhere. Each area has its own `AGENTS.md` (aim for
~8k chars; `agent/subdirectory_hints.py` delivers up to 32k and truncates head/tail with a warning
past that); see the **routing table** at the end and read the area file before editing in that area.

**Never give up on the right solution.**

## What Hermes Is

Hermes is a personal AI agent that runs the same agent core across a CLI, a messaging
gateway (Telegram, Discord, Slack, ~20 platforms), a TUI, and an Electron desktop app. It
learns across sessions (memory + skills), delegates to subagents, runs scheduled jobs, and
drives a real terminal and browser. It is extended primarily through **plugins and skills**,
not by growing the core.

Two invariants shape almost every design decision and are the lens for reviewing any change:

- **Per-conversation prompt caching is sacred.** A long-lived conversation reuses a cached
  prefix every turn. Anything that mutates past context, swaps toolsets, reloads memories, or
  rebuilds the system prompt mid-conversation invalidates that cache and multiplies the user's
  cost. We do not do it; the ONE exception is context compression. Slash commands that mutate
  system-prompt state (skills, tools, memory) must be **cache-aware**: default to deferred
  invalidation (takes effect next session) with an opt-in `--now` flag (`/skills install --now`
  is the canonical pattern).
- **The core is a narrow waist; capability lives at the edges.** Every model tool is sent on
  every API call, so the bar for a new *core* tool is high. New capability should arrive as a
  CLI command + skill, a service-gated tool, or a plugin — not as core surface.

## Contribution Rubric — What We Want / What We Don't

The project's intent layer. It serves humans aiming a contribution AND the automated triage
sweeper, which may only close on `implemented_on_main`, `cannot_reproduce`, or `incoherent`.
Taste-based "out of scope" closes are a human maintainer's call; the sweeper's job is to
recognize design intent and *avoid wrongly closing a legitimate contribution*.

Read the balance right: Hermes ships a **lot**. Most merges are bug fixes to reported
behavior, and the product surface (platforms, providers, models, desktop/TUI features)
expands aggressively on purpose. The restraint below targets the **core agent + model tool
schema**, the one place where every addition is paid for on every API call. "Smallest
footprint" governs *how a capability is wired into the core*, not whether the product may
grow: expansive at the edges, conservative at the waist.

### What we want

- **Fix real bugs, well.** Reproduce the symptom on current `main`, point to the exact line
  where it manifests, and fix the whole bug class — sibling call paths included.
- **Expand reach at the edges.** New adapters, channels, providers, models, desktop/TUI/
  dashboard features land routinely, including large ones — as long as they integrate with
  the existing setup/config UX (`hermes tools`, `hermes setup`, auto-install) rather than
  bolting on a raw env var.
- **Refactor god-files into clean modules.** Huge mechanical `+N/-N` extraction PRs are
  wanted work. "Every line traces to the request" applies to *feature* PRs; a declared
  refactor's request IS the extraction.
- **Keep the core narrow.** Prefer, in order: extend existing code → CLI command + skill →
  service-gated tool (`check_fn`) → plugin → MCP server in the catalog → new core tool (last
  resort). See the Footprint Ladder.
- **Extend, don't duplicate.** Check whether existing infrastructure covers the use case
  before adding a module/manager/hook. When 3+ open PRs integrate the same *category*
  (memory backends, providers, notifiers), design an ABC + orchestrator, wrap the existing
  built-in as the first provider, and turn the competing PRs into plugins against it.
- **Behavior contracts over snapshots.** Tests assert how two pieces of data relate, never
  freeze a current value (see Testing).
- **E2E validation, not just green unit mocks.** Anything touching resolution chains, config
  propagation, security boundaries, remote backends, or file/network I/O must exercise the
  real path with real imports against a temp `HERMES_HOME` — two of them (A→B→A) when the
  change touches profile scope. Mocks hide integration bugs.
- **Cache-, alternation-, and invariant-safe.** Preserve prompt caching, strict role
  alternation (never two same-role messages in a row; never a synthetic user message injected
  mid-loop), and a system prompt byte-stable for the life of a conversation.
- **Contributor credit preserved.** Salvage external work by cherry-picking (rebase-merge) so
  authorship survives; build on top rather than reimplementing.

### What we don't want (rejected even when well-built)

- **Speculative infrastructure.** Hooks/callbacks/extension points with no concrete consumer.
  Adding a hook is easy; removing one after plugins depend on it is hard. A hook with a real,
  stated use case is NOT speculative even if the consumer ships separately.
- **New `HERMES_*` env vars for non-secret config.** `.env` is for secrets only. Behavioral
  settings (timeouts, thresholds, flags, display prefs) go in `config.yaml`; bridge to an
  internal env var in code if the mechanism needs one. Reject "set X in your .env" docs
  unless X is a credential.
- **A new core tool when terminal + file (or a skill) already do the job.** If the only
  barrier is file visibility on a remote backend, fix the mount, not the toolset.
- **Lazy-reading escape hatches on instructional tools.** No `offset`/`limit` pagination on
  tools that load content the agent must read fully (skills, prompts, playbooks) — models
  read page 1 and skip the rest.
- **"Fixes" that destroy the feature they secure.** Read the original intent
  (`git log -p -S`) before restricting behavior; find a fix that preserves the feature.
- **Outbound telemetry / usage attribution without opt-in gating.** No analytics,
  third-party identifier tagging, or attribution tags until a generic user-facing opt-in
  (config gate + setup prompt + `hermes tools` toggle) exists. Park behind a label.
- **Change-detector tests, cache-breaking mid-conversation, dead code wired in without E2E
  proof, plugins that touch core files.** Plugins work within the ABCs/hooks we provide; if
  one needs more, widen the generic plugin surface, never special-case it in core.
- **Third-party products integrated into the core tree.** Observability backends, vendor
  SaaS connectors, analytics dashboards, and other "someone else's product" plugins do NOT
  land under `plugins/` — every one becomes our burden against a fast-moving core for a
  backend we don't own. Ship as a **standalone plugin repo** (`~/.hermes/plugins/` or pip
  entry point), promoted in the Nous Research Discord `#plugins-skills-and-skins`. This is a
  coupling decision, not a quality bar; such PRs are closed with a pointer to publish.

### Before you call it a bug — verify the premise (and when NOT to close)

The most common reason a well-written PR is closed is a **wrong premise** or treating an
**intentional design as a gap**. These patterns tell a reviewer what to scrutinize and tell
the sweeper when a PR is NOT safe to close (when in doubt, leave it open for a human):

- **"Intentional design, not a gap."** Ask whether the isolation IS the design. Profiles are
  independent islands on purpose: a PR adding live config inheritance from the default
  profile was closed because coupling profiles is exactly what the design prevents (`--clone`
  already covers "start from my default"). Read `git log -p -S "<symbol>"` before assuming
  something is unfinished.
- **"The premise doesn't hold against how X actually works."** Trace the real runtime before
  accepting a rationale. Real closes: a rate-limit "re-probe during cooldown" PR (the breaker
  trips only on a *confirmed-empty* bucket, so re-probing hammers a bucket proven empty); a
  usage fix whose new branch **never executes** because an earlier guard already popped the
  state. If you can't point to the exact line where the bug manifests AND show the fix changes
  that line's behavior, the premise is unverified.
- **"The absence was deliberate."** Restoring "missing" `__init__.py` files made a test tree
  importable as a dotted package that shadowed the real plugin and deleted its `register()`
  at import time. The omission was load-bearing.

async def on_gateway_control(command, source, runner):
    if command not in ('stop','new','reset'):return None
    from gateway.slack_workspace import workspace_policy
    policy=workspace_policy(runner,source)
    service=getattr(policy,'vault_service',None)
    if service and policy.authorize_source(source):
        rows=service.store.channel_tasks_for_control(source.scope_id,source.user_id,source.to_dict())
        count=await asyncio.to_thread(service.store.cancel,team=source.scope_id,owner=source.user_id,source=source.to_dict())
        cleanup_pending=await service.channel_control.stop_sources(rows)
        conversation = policy.state['conversations'].get(source.chat_id,{})
        if (service.cloud_browser is not None and getattr(source,'isolated_task',None) is None and
                conversation.get('kind')=='dm'):
            home=policy.home if source.profile=='default' else policy.home/'profiles'/source.profile
            turn=Binding(service,source,'control','',home.resolve(strict=True))
            try:
                await asyncio.to_thread(service.cloud_browser.stop,turn)
            except Exception:
                cleanup_pending=True
        return {'cancelled_pending':count,'cleanup_pending':cleanup_pending}


class VaultService:
    def __init__(self, policy, config):
        self.policy, self.config = policy, config
        self.store = RequestStore(policy.home/'.clanker-vault')
        from .delegation import Delegations
        self.delegations = Delegations(self)
        from .payments import Payments
        self.payments = Payments(self)
        self.loop = None
        self.fill_locks = {}
        self.resume_tasks = {}
        from .channel_tasks import ChannelTasks
        self.channel_tasks = ChannelTasks(self)
        from .channel_control import ChannelControl
        self.channel_control = ChannelControl(self)
        from cloud_browser.service import configured
        self.cloud_browser = configured(self)

    def validate_member(self, team, owner):
        member = self.policy.state['members'].get(owner,{})
        if team!=self.policy.team or member.get('status')!='ready':
            raise AccessError('This Slack account is not authorized for Clanker.',403)
        return member

    def private_home(self, team, owner):
        member = self.validate_member(team,owner)
        profile = member['profile']
        home = self.policy.home if profile=='default' else self.policy.home/'profiles'/profile
        home = home.resolve(strict=True)
        if home!=self.policy.home.resolve() and not home.is_relative_to((self.policy.home/'profiles').resolve()):
            raise AccessError('The private account context is unavailable.',403)
        return home

    def assert_private(self, turn):
        member = self.validate_member(turn.source.scope_id,turn.source.user_id)
        home = self.private_home(turn.source.scope_id,turn.source.user_id)
        conversation = self.policy.state['conversations'].get(turn.source.chat_id,{})
        profile = member['profile']
        if getattr(turn.source,'isolated_task',None) is not None:
            profile = self.channel_tasks.execution_route(turn.source)
            home = self.policy.home / 'profiles' / profile
        if (conversation.get('kind')!='dm' or home!=turn.home.resolve() or
                turn.source.chat_id!=member['dm_id'] or turn.source.profile!=profile or
                not self.policy.authorize_source(turn.source)):
            raise AccessError('Private accounts are available only in your DM with Clanker.',403)
        return home

    async def invitation_members(self, identity):
        self.validate_member(identity['team'], identity['owner'])
        members = []
        client = self.policy.client()
        for uid, member in self.policy.state['members'].items():
            if uid == identity['owner'] or member.get('status') != 'ready':
                continue
            label = member.get('name') or uid
            if hasattr(client, 'users_info'):
                try:
                    user = (await client.users_info(user=uid))['user']
                    label = user.get('profile', {}).get('display_name') or user.get('real_name') or user.get('name') or uid
                except Exception:
                    pass
            members.append({'id': uid, 'name': label})
        return members

    async def revoke_invitation(self, identity, grant_id):
        grant = self.delegations.revoke(identity, grant_id)
        with self.store.connection() as db:
            usages = [dict(row) for row in db.execute(
                'SELECT * FROM credential_grant_usage WHERE grant_id=? AND team=? AND recipient=?',
                (grant_id, grant['team'], grant['recipient']))]
        pending = False
        for usage in usages:
            try:
                await self.channel_control.stop_usage(usage)
            except Exception:
                # Each uncertain context retains its own usage marker. Continue
                # interrupting the other contexts that used this invitation.
                pending = True
        return {'revoked': True, 'cleanup_pending': pending}

    async def set_invitation_access(self, identity, recipient, handles):
        result = await asyncio.to_thread(self.delegations.set_access, identity, recipient, handles)
        pending = False
        # Every revoked grant can have distinct guest task cookie contexts.
        for grant_id in result['revoked']:
            with self.store.connection() as db:
                used = db.execute('SELECT 1 FROM credential_grant_usage WHERE grant_id=?', (grant_id,)).fetchone()
            if used:
                pending = (await self.revoke_invitation(identity, grant_id))['cleanup_pending'] or pending

"""Visible login/code detection and model-blind phone-number autofill."""
import json
import re
import secrets
from dataclasses import replace

from agent.vault_login_classifier import (
    LoginControl, ClassifiedLoginControl, build_inspection_js, build_fill_js, classify_login_control,
    classify_otp_controls, _RE_OTP,
)
from .store import AccessError


# Use the native inspection's visibility and label resolution in every backend.
_CONTROLS = 'JSON.parse(' + build_inspection_js('clanker-login-probe') + ')'
_TEXT = "(c.name+' '+c.label).replace(/([a-z0-9])([A-Z])/g,'$1 $2').replace(/[^a-z0-9]/gi,' ')"
_OTP = "(c.autocomplete.split(/\\s+/).includes('one-time-code') || new RegExp(" + json.dumps(_RE_OTP.pattern) + ", 'i').test(" + _TEXT + '))'
_PHONE = "(!" + _OTP + " && (c.maxLength === null || c.maxLength >= 7) && !c.autocomplete.includes('tel-country-code') && !c.autocomplete.includes('tel-extension') && (c.type === 'tel' || c.autocomplete.split(/\\s+/).some(t => t === 'tel' || t === 'tel-national') || /\\b(phone|telephone|mobile|phonenumber|mobilenumber)\\b/i.test(" + _TEXT + ')))'
PHONE_FIELDS = '(' + _CONTROLS + ').some(c => ' + _PHONE + ')'
PASSWORD_FIELDS = '(' + _CONTROLS + ").some(c => c.type === 'password' && !c.autocomplete.includes('new-password') && !" + _OTP + ')'
LOGIN_FIELDS = '(' + _CONTROLS + ").some(c => !" + _OTP + " && (c.type === 'password' && !c.autocomplete.includes('new-password') || c.type === 'email' || c.autocomplete.split(/\\s+/).includes('username') || /\\b(login|username|identifier)\\b/i.test(c.name) || " + _PHONE + '))'
OTP_FIELDS = '(() => {const controls=' + _CONTROLS + '; if(controls.some(c => ' + _OTP + '))return true; const boxes=controls.filter(c => c.maxLength===1 && ["text","tel","number"].includes(c.type)); return boxes.length>=4 && boxes.length<=8 && boxes.every((c,i) => c.formIndex===boxes[0].formIndex && (!i || c.index===boxes[i-1].index+1));})()'


def normalize_phone(value):
    if not isinstance(value, str) or len(value) > 64 or not re.fullmatch(r'\+?[0-9\s().-]+', value.strip()):
        raise AccessError('Enter a phone number in the format requested by the website.')
    number = re.sub(r'[\s().-]', '', value.strip())
    if not re.fullmatch(r'\+?[0-9]{7,15}', number):
        raise AccessError('Enter a phone number with 7 to 15 digits, including the country code if required.')
    return number


def phone_fills(controls, number):
    controls = normalize_controls(controls)
    otp_indexes = {c.control.index for c in classify_otp_controls(controls)}
    candidates = []
    for control in controls:
        if (control.index in otp_indexes or control.max_length is not None and control.max_length < 7 or
                any(t in control.autocomplete.split() for t in ('tel-country-code', 'tel-extension'))):
            continue
        classified = classify_login_control(control)
        if classified and classified.token == 'tel':
            candidates.append(classified)
        elif (control.type in ('text', 'number', '') and
              (control.autocomplete == 'tel-national' or re.search(r'\b(phone|telephone|mobile|phonenumber|mobilenumber)\b',
               re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', ' ', re.sub(r'([a-z0-9])([A-Z])', r'\1 \2', control.name+' '+control.label).lower())))):
            candidates.append(ClassifiedLoginControl(control, 100 if control.autocomplete=='tel-national' else 70, 'tel'))
    if not candidates:
        raise AccessError('Open the phone-number login field before filling this account.', 409)
    score = max(c.score for c in candidates)
    best = [c for c in candidates if c.score == score]
    if len(best) != 1:
        raise AccessError('The phone-number field is ambiguous. Leave only the intended login form open.', 409)
    target = best[0]
    if target.control.max_length is not None and len(number) > target.control.max_length:
        raise AccessError('The saved number is too long for this field. Save it in the format requested by the website.', 409)
    return [{'index': target.control.index, 'token': 'tel', 'value': number}]


def normalize_controls(controls):
    return [replace(c, name=re.sub(r'([a-z0-9])([A-Z])', r'\1 \2', c.name),
                    label=re.sub(r'([a-z0-9])([A-Z])', r'\1 \2', c.label)) for c in controls]


def sms_otp_controls(controls):
    matched=classify_otp_controls(controls)
    if matched:return matched
    boxes=[c for c in controls if c.max_length==1 and c.type in ('text','tel','number')]
    if (4<=len(boxes)<=8 and len({c.form_index for c in boxes})==1 and
            all(b.index==a.index+1 for a,b in zip(boxes,boxes[1:]))):
        return [ClassifiedLoginControl(c,70,'one-time-code') for c in boxes]
    return []


def sms_code_fills(controls, code):
    from agent.vault_login_classifier import build_otp_fills
    matched=sms_otp_controls(controls)
    if not matched:
        raise AccessError('Open the SMS verification-code field before entering the code.', 409)
    boxes=[c for c in matched if c.control.max_length==1]
    if boxes and len(boxes)!=len(code):
        raise AccessError('The SMS code length does not match the website\'s verification fields.', 409)
    fills=build_otp_fills(matched,code)
    lengths={c.index:c.max_length for c in controls}
    if any(lengths[f['index']] is not None and len(f['value'])>lengths[f['index']] for f in fills):
        raise AccessError('The SMS code is too long for the website\'s verification field.', 409)
    return fills


def local_fill(turn, access, *, code=None):
    """Fill phone or SMS code without exposing the value to the model."""
    from tools import browser_vault_tool as native
    from agent.redact import register_vault_redaction_value
    service = turn.service
    service.assert_private(turn)
    service.delegations.resolve(turn, access.handle)
    service.delegations.check_execution(turn)
    supervisor = native._ensure_supervisor(turn.task_id)
    if supervisor is None:
        raise AccessError('Start this task\'s private browser before filling the login.', 409)
    from seatbelt.context import Context
    Context(turn.home).owned_cdp(supervisor.cdp_url)
    focused = supervisor.focus_page(access.meta.origin, accept=OTP_FIELDS if code is not None else PHONE_FIELDS)
    if not focused.get('ok') or native._current_page_origin(turn.task_id) != access.meta.origin:
        raise AccessError('Open the matching account phone or verification form before filling it.', 403)
    nonce = secrets.token_hex(8)
    inspected = native._eval_js(turn.task_id, build_inspection_js(nonce))
    raw = native._parse_json_result(inspected.get('result')) if inspected.get('success') else None
    if isinstance(raw, str):raw = native._parse_json_result(raw)
    if not isinstance(raw, list):
        raise AccessError('The phone login form could not be inspected.', 409)
    controls = normalize_controls([LoginControl.from_dict(c) for c in raw if isinstance(c, dict)])
    value = code if code is not None else access.secret()['phone_number']
    fills = sms_code_fills(controls, value) if code is not None else phone_fills(controls, value)
    if not fills:
        raise AccessError('Open the SMS verification-code field before entering the code.', 409)
    register_vault_redaction_value(value)
    if code is None:register_vault_redaction_value(value.lstrip('+'))
    service.delegations.record_browser_use(turn, access)
    filled = native._eval_js_secret(turn.task_id, build_fill_js(fills, expected_origin=access.meta.origin, nonce=nonce))
    data = native._parse_json_result(filled.get('result')) if filled.get('success') else None
    if isinstance(data, str):data = native._parse_json_result(data)
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get('refused') or not data.get('filled'):
        raise AccessError('The phone login fill was not confirmed.', 409)
    return {'success': True, 'filled_fields': data['filled'], 'origin': access.meta.origin,
            'next': ('Continue the website login and verify its result.' if code is not None else
                     'Use the website to request its SMS code, then call clanker_vault_enter_code with this handle. Never read or echo the filled phone number.')}

"""Passwordless phone login: owner-bound HTTP, encrypted storage and scoped resume."""
import asyncio
import json
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch

import pytest
from aiohttp.test_utils import TestClient, TestServer

from test_clanker_vault import service
from agent.vault_login_classifier import LoginControl
from agent.vault_store import VaultStore, VaultError
from gateway.config import Platform
from gateway.session import SessionSource
from vault.service import Binding
from vault.store import RequestStore, AccessError
from vault.web import VaultWeb
from vault.login import normalize_phone, phone_fills, sms_otp_controls, sms_code_fills


def turn(service, owner='UA', task='phone-task'):
    source=SessionSource(Platform.SLACK,'D'+owner,user_id=owner,scope_id='TT',profile=owner,thread_id='100.1')
    return Binding(service,source,task,'Read my account status.',service.private_home('TT',owner))


def request(service, owner='UA', task='phone-task'):
    actor=turn(service,owner,task)
    return service.store.create(team='TT',owner=owner,home=actor.home,task_id=actor.task_id,
        source=actor.source.to_dict(),task=actor.message,kind='login',label='SMS account',
        origin='https://accounts.example.com',login_method='sms')


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_phone_and_sms_forms_are_owner_bound_encrypted_durable_and_resume_a_b_a(service):
    events=[]
    async def receive(event):
        events.append(event);event._gateway_accepted=True
        service.policy.adapter._session_tasks[service.policy.adapter._event_session_key(event)]=asyncio.create_task(asyncio.sleep(0))
    service.policy.adapter.handle_message=receive
    service.policy.adapter.gateway_runner=SimpleNamespace(_active_sessions={},session_store=SimpleNamespace(get_session_key=lambda s:'phone-session'))
    service.loop=asyncio.get_running_loop()
    client=TestClient(TestServer(VaultWeb(service,service.config).app));await client.start_server()
    try:
        for index,owner in enumerate(('UA','UB','UA')):
            row=request(service,owner,'phone-task-'+str(index))
            data={'id':row['id'],'token':service.store.token(row['id'])}
            sid=service.store.new_session('TT',owner)
            headers={'Origin':'https://vault.example','Cookie':'__Host-clanker='+sid,
                     'X-CSRF-Token':service.store.session(sid)['csrf']}
            other=service.store.new_session('TT','UB' if owner=='UA' else 'UA')
            wrong=headers|{'Cookie':'__Host-clanker='+other,'X-CSRF-Token':service.store.session(other)['csrf']}
            response=await client.post('/api/request',json=data,headers=headers)
            assert response.status==200
            assert (await response.json())['login_method']=='sms'
            phone='+1202555010'+str(index)
            for invalid in ({'phone_number':phone,'password':'x'}, {'phone_number':'555'},
                            {'phone_number':phone,'owner':'UB'}, {'identifier':phone}, {'phone_number':None}):
                assert (await client.post('/api/save',json=data|{'fields':invalid},headers=headers)).status==400
            assert (await client.post('/api/save',json=data|{'fields':{'phone_number':phone}},headers=wrong)).status==403
            assert (await client.post('/api/save',json=data|{'fields':{'phone_number':phone}},headers=headers|{'X-CSRF-Token':'wrong'})).status==403
            response=await client.post('/api/save',json=data|{'fields':{'phone_number':phone}},headers=headers)
            assert response.status==200
            assert phone not in await response.text()
            assert (await client.post('/api/save',json=data|{'fields':{'phone_number':phone}},headers=headers)).status==410
            service.store=RequestStore(service.store.directory)
            saved=next(r for r in service.store.pending_resumes() if r['id']==row['id'])
            vault=VaultStore(service.private_home('TT',owner)/'vault')
            meta=vault.get_meta(saved['handle'])
            assert meta.login_method=='sms' and meta.identifier=='••••'+phone[-4:]
            assert vault.resolve_secret(meta.id)=={'phone_number':phone}
            assert phone not in json.dumps(service.delegations.items('TT',owner))
            assert phone.encode() not in service.store.path.read_bytes()
            assert phone.encode() not in vault._vault_path.read_bytes()
            await service.drain();await asyncio.gather(*list(service.resume_tasks.values()))
            assert events[-1].source.user_id==owner and events[-1].source.chat_id=='D'+owner
            assert meta.id in events[-1].text and phone not in events[-1].text
            waiting=await service.request_code(turn(service,owner,'phone-task-'+str(index)),meta)
            code_data={'id':waiting['request_id'],'token':service.store.token(waiting['request_id'])}
            response=await client.post('/api/request',json=code_data,headers=headers)
            assert (await response.json())['login_method']=='sms'
            assert (await client.post('/api/code',json=code_data|{'fields':{'code':'829471'}},headers=wrong)).status==403
            response=await client.post('/api/code',json=code_data|{'fields':{'code':'829471'}},headers=headers)
            assert response.status==200 and '829471' not in await response.text()
            assert b'829471' not in service.store.path.read_bytes()
            service.store=RequestStore(service.store.directory)
            await service.drain();await asyncio.gather(*list(service.resume_tasks.values()))
            assert events[-1].source.user_id==owner and 'clanker_vault_enter_code' in events[-1].text
            args=dict(team='TT',owner=owner,home=service.private_home('TT',owner),task_id='phone-task-'+str(index),handle=meta.id,origin=meta.origin)
            assert service.store.consume_code(**(args|{'origin':'https://other.example.com'})) is None
            assert service.store.consume_code(**(args|{'owner':'OTHER'})) is None
            assert service.store.consume_code(**args)=='829471'
            assert service.store.consume_code(**args) is None
    finally:await client.close()


def test_phone_login_replacement_compares_full_number_and_preserves_other_accounts(service):
    identity={'team':'TT','owner':'UA'}
    handles=[]
    for index,number in enumerate(('+12025550101','+13035550101','+12025550101')):
        row=request(service,task=str(index))
        handles.append(service.save_login(row['id'],service.store.token(row['id']),identity,{'phone_number':number}).id)
    vault=VaultStore(service.private_home('TT','UA')/'vault')
    assert vault.get_meta(handles[0]) is None
    assert vault.get_meta(handles[1]) and vault.get_meta(handles[2])
    assert len(vault.list_items())==2


def test_phone_login_native_validation_crash_adoption_and_password_compatibility(service):
    row=request(service);vault=VaultStore(service.private_home('TT','UA')/'vault')
    for secret in ({'login_method':'sms','phone_number':'invalid'}, {'login_method':'sms','phone_number':'+12025550101','password':'x'},
                   {'login_method':'other','phone_number':'+12025550101'}):
        with pytest.raises(VaultError):vault.add_item('login','SMS account',secret,origin=row['origin'])
    meta=vault.add_item('login',row['label'],{'login_method':'sms','phone_number':'+12025550101'},
                        origin=row['origin'],idempotency_key='clanker-access:'+row['id'])
    with pytest.raises(VaultError):vault.add_item('login',row['label'],{'login_method':'sms','phone_number':'+13035550101'},
                        origin=row['origin'],idempotency_key='clanker-access:'+row['id'])
    restored=RequestStore(service.store.directory);restored.recover_saves()
    assert restored.pending_resumes()[0]['handle']==meta.id
    normal=vault.add_item('login','Password account',{'identifier_type':'email','identifier':'a@example.invalid','password':'REDACTED'},origin=row['origin'])
    assert normal.login_method=='password' and 'login_method' not in normal.to_dict()


@pytest.mark.parametrize('raw,expected',[('+1 (202) 555-0101','+12025550101'),('202 555 0101','2025550101')])
def test_phone_format_normalization(raw,expected):assert normalize_phone(raw)==expected


def test_phone_classifier_excludes_codes_country_codes_and_ambiguous_fields():
    def c(index,name='',type='tel',autocomplete='',max_length=None):
        return LoginControl(autocomplete,0,index,'',name,type,max_length)
    phone=c(0,'mobile')
    assert phone_fills([phone,c(1,'otp',max_length=6),c(2,autocomplete='tel-country-code',max_length=3)],'2025550101')[0]['index']==0
    assert phone_fills([c(0,'mobileNumber','text')],'2025550101')[0]['index']==0
    for controls in ([c(0,'phoneOtp',max_length=32)], [c(0,'otp',autocomplete='one-time-code')], [phone,c(1,'phone')]):
        with pytest.raises(AccessError):phone_fills(controls,'2025550101')
    with pytest.raises(AccessError):phone_fills([c(0,'mobile',max_length=10)],'+12025550101')


def test_unlabelled_split_sms_widget_requires_one_adjacent_group():
    boxes=[LoginControl('',0,i,'','digit'+str(i),'tel',1) for i in range(6)]
    assert len(sms_otp_controls(boxes))==6
    assert not sms_otp_controls(boxes[:3])
    assert not sms_otp_controls(boxes[:2]+boxes[3:])
    assert not sms_otp_controls(boxes+[LoginControl('',1,6,'','digit6','tel',1)])


def test_sms_code_cannot_be_truncated_into_wrong_length_widgets():
    boxes=[LoginControl('one-time-code',0,i,'','otp'+str(i),'tel',1) for i in range(6)]
    assert ''.join(fill['value'] for fill in sms_code_fills(boxes,'829471'))=='829471'
    for code in ('1234','12345678'):
        with pytest.raises(AccessError):sms_code_fills(boxes,code)
    field=[LoginControl('one-time-code',0,0,'','otp','tel',6)]
    with pytest.raises(AccessError):sms_code_fills(field,'12345678')


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_sms_codes_are_expired_and_revoked_with_invited_access(service):
    row=request(service);identity={'team':'TT','owner':'UA'}
    meta=service.save_login(row['id'],service.store.token(row['id']),identity,{'phone_number':'+12025550101'})
    grant=service.delegations.invite(identity,meta.id,'UB')['id']
    guest=turn(service,'UB');access=service.delegations.resolve(guest,grant)
    waiting=await service.request_code(guest,meta,access=access)
    with pytest.raises(AccessError):service.save_code(waiting['request_id'],service.store.token(waiting['request_id']),{'team':'TT','owner':'UB'},{'code':'829471'})
    service.save_code(waiting['request_id'],service.store.token(waiting['request_id']),identity,{'code':'829471'})
    args=dict(team='TT',owner='UB',home=guest.home,task_id=guest.task_id,handle=grant,origin=meta.origin)
    assert service.store.consume_code(**args)=='829471'
    waiting=await service.request_code(guest,meta,access=access)
    service.delegations.revoke(identity,grant)
    with pytest.raises(AccessError):service.save_code(waiting['request_id'],service.store.token(waiting['request_id']),identity,{'code':'829471'})
    assert service.store.consume_code(**args) is None
    own=await service.request_code(turn(service),meta)
    service.save_code(own['request_id'],service.store.token(own['request_id']),identity,{'code':'829471'})
    stored=service.store.get(own['request_id'],service.store.token(own['request_id']),waiting=False)
    service.store.clock=lambda:stored['expires']+1
    assert service.store.consume_code(**(args|{'owner':'UA','home':service.private_home('TT','UA'),'handle':meta.id})) is None
"""Isolated loopback-only UI fixture. No Slack connection and no real accounts.

The fixture entry route creates a test-owner cookie. It is absent from the
production application; the production form always authenticates through Slack.
"""
import asyncio
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import tempfile
from types import SimpleNamespace
from urllib.parse import urlencode
from aiohttp import web

ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path[:0]=[str(ROOT/'runtime'),str(ROOT/'hermes')]
from gateway.config import Platform
from gateway.session import SessionSource
from agent.vault_store import VaultStore
from vault.service import VaultService
from vault.web import VaultWeb


async def main():
    parser=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--port',type=int,default=8769,help='Loopback-only fixture port (default 8769).')
    args=parser.parse_args()
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT/'.local/hermes-lab',prefix='vault-ui-fixture-') as directory:
        home=Path(directory);(home/'profiles/DEMO').mkdir(parents=True)
        policy=SimpleNamespace(home=home,team='TFIXTURE',state={'members':{'DEMO':{'profile':'DEMO','status':'ready','dm_id':'DDEMO'}}})
        service=VaultService(policy,{'public_url':'http://127.0.0.1:'+str(args.port),'client_id':'fixture','local_test':True,'port':args.port})
        source=SessionSource(Platform.SLACK,'DDEMO',user_id='DEMO',scope_id='TFIXTURE',profile='DEMO',thread_id='1.1')
        app=VaultWeb(service,service.config)
        async def entry(request):
            kind=request.query.get('kind','login')
            if kind not in ('login','code','api_key','payment'):raise web.HTTPBadRequest()
            login_method=request.query.get('login_method','password') if kind in ('login','code') else 'password'
            handle=None
            checkout=None
            if kind=='payment':
                if request.query.get('saved')=='1':
                    handle=VaultStore(service.private_home('TFIXTURE','DEMO')/'vault').add_item('payment','Payment card',
                        {'card_number':'4242424242424242','exp_month':'12','exp_year':'2030'},origin='https://www.swiggy.com').id
                checkout={'order':{'merchant':'Swiggy','summary':'KFC: Chicken Zinger Classic with Cheese ×1 and Zinger Pro ×1. Delivery: Home 2.',
                    'amount_minor':69900,'currency':'INR'},'snapshot':{'origin':'https://www.swiggy.com','url':'https://www.swiggy.com/checkout',
                    'text':'KFC · Demo checkout\nChicken Zinger Classic with Cheese ×1\nZinger Pro ×1\nTotal including fees: ₹699.00\nPay ₹699.00',
                    'button':'Pay ₹699.00','browser':'fixture-only'},'nonce':'fixture-only'}
            if kind=='code':
                meta=VaultStore(service.private_home('TFIXTURE','DEMO')/'vault').add_item('login','Fixture verification',
                    {'login_method':'sms','phone_number':'2025550101'} if login_method=='sms' else
                    {'identifier':'demo@example.invalid','identifier_type':'email','password':'REDACTED'},
                    origin='https://www.swiggy.com' if login_method=='sms' else 'https://accounts.google.com')
                handle=meta.id
            label=request.query.get('label','Fixture API key') if kind=='api_key' else 'Payment card' if kind=='payment' else 'Swiggy login · www.swiggy.com' if login_method=='sms' else 'Google login · accounts.google.com'
            row=service.store.create(team='TFIXTURE',owner='DEMO',home=service.private_home('TFIXTURE','DEMO'),task_id='fixture',source=source.to_dict(),
                task='Controlled UI fixture only.',kind=kind,label=label,origin='https://www.swiggy.com' if kind=='payment' or login_method=='sms' else 'https://api.example.invalid' if kind=='api_key' else 'https://accounts.google.com',identifier='' if kind in ('api_key','payment') or login_method=='sms' else 'demo@example.invalid',handle=handle,checkout=checkout,login_method=login_method)
            sid=service.store.new_session('TFIXTURE','DEMO')
            response=web.Response(status=302,headers={'Location':'/vault/fill#'+urlencode({'r':row['id'],'token':service.store.token(row['id'])})})
            response.set_cookie('__Host-clanker',sid,secure=True,httponly=True,samesite='Lax',path='/')
            return response
        app.app.router.add_get('/fixture',entry)
        async def payment_otp_preview(request):
            # Display-only prototype: no OTP submission or bank integration.
            return web.Response(text=(ROOT/'verification/previews/payment-otp.html').read_text(),content_type='text/html')
        app.app.router.add_get('/fixture/payment-otp',payment_otp_preview)
        # Exercise the real UI failure handling, preserving entered secrets.
        original=service.save_login
        attempts=0
        def transient_save(*args):
            nonlocal attempts
            attempts+=1
            if attempts==1:raise RuntimeError('Controlled transient failure')
            return original(*args)
        service.save_login=transient_save
        original_api=service.save_api_key
        api_attempts=0
        def transient_api_save(*args):
            nonlocal api_attempts
            api_attempts+=1
            if api_attempts==1:raise RuntimeError('Controlled transient failure')
            return original_api(*args)

# agent/ — AIAgent, turn loop, prompt, compression

Applies on top of the root `AGENTS.md` (prompt-caching invariant, facade + siblings rules).

## Shape

`run_agent.py` is the public facade: `AIAgent` is assembled from mixins (`agent/turn_facade.py`,
`client_lifecycle.py`, `stream_delivery.py`, `session_persistence.py`, `compression_facade.py`, ...).
Construction runs `agent/agent_init.py::init_agent`; a turn is
`agent/conversation_loop.py::run_conversation`, which `AIAgent.run_conversation` forwards to after
taking the session turn lease (`turn_facade_lease.py`). `AIAgent.__init__` takes ~60 parameters
(credentials, routing, callbacks, session context, budget, credential pool, ...) — read
`run_agent.py` for the list; the subset you usually touch: `base_url`, `api_key`, `provider`,
`api_mode` (`"chat_completions" | "codex_responses" | ...`), `model` (empty → resolved from
config/provider later), `max_iterations` (default 500, shared with subagents),
`enabled_toolsets`/`disabled_toolsets`, `quiet_mode`, `save_trajectories`, `platform`
(`"cli"`, `"telegram"`, ...), `session_id`, `skip_context_files`, `skip_memory`, `credential_pool`.
`chat(message) -> str` is the simple interface; `run_conversation(user_message, system_message=None,
conversation_history=None, task_id=None) -> dict` returns `final_response` + `messages`.

## Agent loop (`agent/conversation_loop.py` + `agent/turn_*.py`)

Entirely synchronous, with interrupt checks, budget tracking, and a one-turn grace call:

```python
while (api_call_count < self.max_iterations and self.iteration_budget.remaining > 0) \
        or self._budget_grace_call:
    if self._interrupt_requested: break
    response = client.chat.completions.create(model=model, messages=messages, tools=tool_schemas)
    if response.tool_calls:
        for tc in response.tool_calls:
            messages.append(tool_result_message(handle_function_call(tc.name, tc.args, task_id)))
        api_call_count += 1
    else:
        return response.content
```

Each phase of an iteration is its own sibling, so a change to (say) overflow handling touches one
~600-line file: `turn_preflight*`, `turn_iteration_prep`, `turn_request_assembly`/`turn_api_request`,
`turn_api_call`, `turn_api_error`, `turn_response_intake`/`turn_response_check`,
`turn_empty_response`, `turn_tool_round`/`turn_tool_validation`, `turn_overflow`,
`turn_truncation`, `turn_context_compaction`, `turn_recovery`, `turn_recovery_autorecover`
(post-exhaustion wait-and-retry ladder), `turn_retry_state`,
`turn_stop_gates`, `turn_liveness`, `turn_usage`, `turn_final_response`, `turn_finalizer`,
`turn_summary`. Find the phase with `grep -rn "def X" agent/turn_*.py`.

Messages use OpenAI format `{"role": "system|user|assistant|tool", ...}`; reasoning content is stored
in `assistant_msg["reasoning"]`.

**Agent-level tools** (`todo`, `memory`, ...) are intercepted by `agent/tool_executor.py` through the
`INLINE_TOOL_EXECUTORS` table in `agent/inline_tool_executors.py` before `handle_function_call()`.
Adding one: register in that table (no `if name == ...` chain); `tools/todo_tool.py` is the pattern.

## Message-flow invariants (every change is reviewed against these)

- **Prompt caching must not break.** Never alter past context, change toolsets, reload memories,
  or rebuild the system prompt mid-conversation. The system prompt is byte-stable for the life of
  a conversation; the ONLY context mutation is compression. Anything that must inject content
  mid-conversation rides a **user message or tool result**, never the system prompt: skill slash
  commands (`agent/skill_commands.py`) inject as a user message; subdirectory `AGENTS.md` hints
  (`agent/subdirectory_hints.py`) append to the tool result (head+tail truncated past `_MAX_HINT_CHARS = 32_000`;
  the truncation is logged, never queued as a chat status warning — `context_file_max_chars` does not raise that cap).
- **Strict role alternation.** Never two same-role messages in a row; never a synthetic user
  message injected mid-loop. The one exception is `/steer`, delivered as a standalone user row
  after a tool result (`assistant(tool_calls) → tool → user` is legal on every provider path) —
  never smeared onto the already-persisted tool row, which append-only persistence would leave
  divergent from the live request. Cron deliveries live in their own session for this reason.
- **Context files** (`agent/prompt_builder.py`) load from the CWD only at startup and are capped
  (`CONTEXT_FILE_MAX_CHARS` / dynamic cap from the context window / `context_file_max_chars`).
  Never load an install-tree `AGENTS.md` as project context (PR #64611); subdirectory hints reject
  paths outside the working dir so `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` / `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` never mix in.
- **`_last_resolved_tool_names` is a process-global in `model_tools.py`.** `_run_single_child()`
  in `tools/delegate_tool.py` saves/restores it around subagent execution; code reading it may see
  a temporarily stale value during child runs.

## Compression (`agent/compression_facade.py`, `conversation_compression.py`, `turn_context_compaction.py`)

Manual `/compress` on every surface (CLI, gateway, TUI, ACP) runs through
`agent/conversation_compression_manual.py::compress_now` (one parser for `here [N]` / focus /
`--preview` / `--aggressive`; surfaces only parse their own argv, install `after_messages` and render).

Two layers: gateway session hygiene (85% threshold) and the agent `ContextCompressor` (50%,
configurable; per-model overrides; failure cooldown after provider-proven overflow). The algorithm
prunes old tool results first (no LLM call), then picks boundaries, then generates a structured
summary with the `auxiliary` compression model. In-place compaction keeps a single stable session
id; native Responses/Codex compaction paths are provider-specific. A stalled summary stream retries
once on `auxiliary.compression.fallback_chain`, and a repeated stall (a stall-class failure already on
the cooldown ladder) ends with the deterministic fallback summary through the same pipeline — never a
prune committed outside the lease/fence. Compression is the sanctioned
cache break — keep it the only one. Full detail:
`website/docs/developer-guide/context-compression-and-caching.md`.

## Model and provider resolution

- Runtime provider/model resolution and its precedence: `website/docs/developer-guide/provider-runtime.md`.
  Provider profiles are plugins (`plugins/model-providers/<name>/`, see `plugins/AGENTS.md`);
  `agent/model_metadata.py` holds context lengths and capabilities.
- **Auxiliary (side-LLM) work** — curator, vision, embedding, title generation, session_search,
  compression — resolves through `agent/auxiliary_client.py::_resolve_auto_route`; each task can pin
  its own `provider/model/base_url/reasoning_effort` under `auxiliary:` in config.yaml.
  Every physical attempt funnels through `_relay_sync_completion` / `_relay_async_completion` /
  `_relay_sync_stream`, where `agent/auxiliary_hooks.py` emits `pre_auxiliary_call` /
  `post_auxiliary_call` (observer-only, fail-open, `aux_task` set); the main-loop
  `pre/post_api_request` events must NOT fire for aux calls (#79733).
- Fallback models and credential pools are resolution-chain code: E2E them with real imports
  against a temp `HERMES_HOME`, not mocks (root rubric).

## Memory, context engines, curator

`agent/memory_provider.py` (ABC) + `agent/memory_manager.py` (orchestrator) drive memory-provider
plugins; `agent/context_engine.py` drives context-engine plugins; `agent/image_gen_provider.py`
image-gen plugins (all in `plugins/AGENTS.md`). `agent/curator.py` + `curator_backup.py` implement
the skill curator (`skills/AGENTS.md`). Cron sessions pass `skip_memory=True` by default — memory
providers intentionally do not run during cron.

- End-of-session memory extraction and provider `on_session_end` run wherever the session ends —
  turn, eviction, shutdown, `tui_gateway` teardown — and the CALLER binds the owning profile's scope
  first (`_run_release_in_profile_scope`, `_session_profile_runtime_scope`); the agent never derives
  its home from `os.environ` at flush time (`Path(_session_db.db_path).parent` is the ground truth).
  Provider background work starts through `memory_provider.py::spawn_context_thread` (copies the
  contextvars), never a bare `threading.Thread`; `title_generator.py` is the shape.
- `agent/secret_scope.py::get_secret` fails closed (`UnscopedSecretError`) only after
  `set_multiplex_active(True)`; the gateway, cron, migrate and `serve` set it. A new multi-home host
  must too, or every guard is silently off. Isolation is BETWEEN profiles; children inherit via
  `copy_context`; a child's `UnscopedSecretError` is a spawn-site bug, never grounds for an
  `os.getenv` fallthrough. Delegated children carry `delegation_context.py::
  DELEGATED_CHILD_ENV_MARKER` valued as the fenced Kanban board root, not a bare flag.

## Tests

Loop/phase tests go in `tests/agent/`; patch the binding the phase actually reads (siblings often
`from run_agent import X` inside the function — root "patch where production reads"). Assert
message-shape invariants (alternation, byte-stable system prompt) rather than snapshotting prompt
text.

Long-form: `website/docs/developer-guide/agent-loop.md`, `prompt-assembly.md`,
`context-compression-and-caching.md`, `provider-runtime.md`, `session-storage.md`,
`subagent-lifecycle-api.md`.

# agent/ — AIAgent, turn loop, prompt, compression

Applies on top of the root `AGENTS.md` (prompt-caching invariant, facade + siblings rules).

## Shape

`run_agent.py` is the public facade: `AIAgent` is assembled from mixins (`agent/turn_facade.py`,
`client_lifecycle.py`, `stream_delivery.py`, `session_persistence.py`, `compression_facade.py`, ...).
Construction runs `agent/agent_init.py::init_agent`; a turn is
`agent/conversation_loop.py::run_conversation`, which `AIAgent.run_conversation` forwards to after
taking the session turn lease (`turn_facade_lease.py`). `AIAgent.__init__` takes ~60 parameters
(credentials, routing, callbacks, session context, budget, credential pool, ...) — read
`run_agent.py` for the list; the subset you usually touch: `base_url`, `api_key`, `provider`,
`api_mode` (`"chat_completions" | "codex_responses" | ...`), `model` (empty → resolved from
config/provider later), `max_iterations` (default 500, shared with subagents),
`enabled_toolsets`/`disabled_toolsets`, `quiet_mode`, `save_trajectories`, `platform`
(`"cli"`, `"telegram"`, ...), `session_id`, `skip_context_files`, `skip_memory`, `credential_pool`.
`chat(message) -> str` is the simple interface; `run_conversation(user_message, system_message=None,
conversation_history=None, task_id=None) -> dict` returns `final_response` + `messages`.

## Agent loop (`agent/conversation_loop.py` + `agent/turn_*.py`)

Entirely synchronous, with interrupt checks, budget tracking, and a one-turn grace call:

```python
while (api_call_count < self.max_iterations and self.iteration_budget.remaining > 0) \
        or self._budget_grace_call:
    if self._interrupt_requested: break
    response = client.chat.completions.create(model=model, messages=messages, tools=tool_schemas)
    if response.tool_calls:
        for tc in response.tool_calls:
            messages.append(tool_result_message(handle_function_call(tc.name, tc.args, task_id)))
        api_call_count += 1
    else:
        return response.content
```

Each phase of an iteration is its own sibling, so a change to (say) overflow handling touches one
~600-line file: `turn_preflight*`, `turn_iteration_prep`, `turn_request_assembly`/`turn_api_request`,
`turn_api_call`, `turn_api_error`, `turn_response_intake`/`turn_response_check`,
`turn_empty_response`, `turn_tool_round`/`turn_tool_validation`, `turn_overflow`,
`turn_truncation`, `turn_context_compaction`, `turn_recovery`, `turn_recovery_autorecover`
(post-exhaustion wait-and-retry ladder), `turn_retry_state`,
`turn_stop_gates`, `turn_liveness`, `turn_usage`, `turn_final_response`, `turn_finalizer`,
`turn_summary`. Find the phase with `grep -rn "def X" agent/turn_*.py`.

Messages use OpenAI format `{"role": "system|user|assistant|tool", ...}`; reasoning content is stored
in `assistant_msg["reasoning"]`.

**Agent-level tools** (`todo`, `memory`, ...) are intercepted by `agent/tool_executor.py` through the
`INLINE_TOOL_EXECUTORS` table in `agent/inline_tool_executors.py` before `handle_function_call()`.
Adding one: register in that table (no `if name == ...` chain); `tools/todo_tool.py` is the pattern.

## Message-flow invariants (every change is reviewed against these)

- **Prompt caching must not break.** Never alter past context, change toolsets, reload memories,
  or rebuild the system prompt mid-conversation. The system prompt is byte-stable for the life of
  a conversation; the ONLY context mutation is compression. Anything that must inject content
  mid-conversation rides a **user message or tool result**, never the system prompt: skill slash
  commands (`agent/skill_commands.py`) inject as a user message; subdirectory `AGENTS.md` hints
  (`agent/subdirectory_hints.py`) append to the tool result (head+tail truncated past `_MAX_HINT_CHARS = 32_000`;
  the truncation is logged, never queued as a chat status warning — `context_file_max_chars` does not raise that cap).
- **Strict role alternation.** Never two same-role messages in a row; never a synthetic user
  message injected mid-loop. The one exception is `/steer`, delivered as a standalone user row
  after a tool result (`assistant(tool_calls) → tool → user` is legal on every provider path) —
  never smeared onto the already-persisted tool row, which append-only persistence would leave
  divergent from the live request. Cron deliveries live in their own session for this reason.
- **Context files** (`agent/prompt_builder.py`) load from the CWD only at startup and are capped
  (`CONTEXT_FILE_MAX_CHARS` / dynamic cap from the context window / `context_file_max_chars`).
  Never load an install-tree `AGENTS.md` as project context (PR #64611); subdirectory hints reject
  paths outside the working dir so `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` / `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` never mix in.
- **`_last_resolved_tool_names` is a process-global in `model_tools.py`.** `_run_single_child()`
  in `tools/delegate_tool.py` saves/restores it around subagent execution; code reading it may see
  a temporarily stale value during child runs.

## Compression (`agent/compression_facade.py`, `conversation_compression.py`, `turn_context_compaction.py`)

Manual `/compress` on every surface (CLI, gateway, TUI, ACP) runs through
`agent/conversation_compression_manual.py::compress_now` (one parser for `here [N]` / focus /
`--preview` / `--aggressive`; surfaces only parse their own argv, install `after_messages` and render).

Two layers: gateway session hygiene (85% threshold) and the agent `ContextCompressor` (50%,
configurable; per-model overrides; failure cooldown after provider-proven overflow). The algorithm
prunes old tool results first (no LLM call), then picks boundaries, then generates a structured
summary with the `auxiliary` compression model. In-place compaction keeps a single stable session
id; native Responses/Codex compaction paths are provider-specific. A stalled summary stream retries
once on `auxiliary.compression.fallback_chain`, and a repeated stall (a stall-class failure already on
the cooldown ladder) ends with the deterministic fallback summary through the same pipeline — never a
prune committed outside the lease/fence. Compression is the sanctioned
cache break — keep it the only one. Full detail:
`website/docs/developer-guide/context-compression-and-caching.md`.

## Model and provider resolution

- Runtime provider/model resolution and its precedence: `website/docs/developer-guide/provider-runtime.md`.
  Provider profiles are plugins (`plugins/model-providers//`, see `plugins/AGENTS.md`);
  `agent/model_metadata.py` holds context lengths and capabilities.
- **Auxiliary (side-LLM) work** — curator, vision, embedding, title generation, session_search,
  compression — resolves through `agent/auxiliary_client.py::_resolve_auto_route`; each task can pin
  its own `provider/model/base_url/reasoning_effort` under `auxiliary:` in config.yaml.
  Every physical attempt funnels through `_relay_sync_completion` / `_relay_async_completion` /
  `_relay_sync_stream`, where `agent/auxiliary_hooks.py` emits `pre_auxiliary_call` /
  `post_auxiliary_call` (observer-only, fail-open, `aux_task` set); the main-loop
  `pre/post_api_request` events must NOT fire for aux calls (#79733).
- Fallback models and credential pools are resolution-chain code: E2E them with real imports
  against a temp `HERMES_HOME`, not mocks (root rubric).

## Memory, context engines, curator

`agent/memory_provider.py` (ABC) + `agent/memory_manager.py` (orchestrator) drive memory-provider
plugins; `agent/context_engine.py` drives context-engine plugins; `agent/image_gen_provider.py`
image-gen plugins (all in `plugins/AGENTS.md`). `agent/curator.py` + `curator_backup.py` implement
the skill curator (`skills/AGENTS.md`). Cron sessions pass `skip_memory=True` by default — memory
providers intentionally do not run during cron.

- End-of-session memory extraction and provider `on_session_end` run wherever the session ends —
  turn, eviction, shutdown, `tui_gateway` teardown — and the CALLER binds the owning profile's scope
  first (`_run_release_in_profile_scope`, `_session_profile_runtime_scope`); the agent never derives
  its home from `os.environ` at flush time (`Path(_session_db.db_path).parent` is the ground truth).
  Provider background work starts through `memory_provider.py::spawn_context_thread` (copies the
  contextvars), never a bare `threading.Thread`; `title_generator.py` is the shape.
- `agent/secret_scope.py::get_secret` fails closed (`UnscopedSecretError`) only after
  `set_multiplex_active(True)`; the gateway, cron, migrate and `serve` set it. A new multi-home host
  must too, or every guard is silently off. Isolation is BETWEEN profiles; children inherit via
  `copy_context`; a child's `UnscopedSecretError` is a spawn-site bug, never grounds for an
  `os.getenv` fallthrough. Delegated children carry `delegation_context.py::
  DELEGATED_CHILD_ENV_MARKER` valued as the fenced Kanban board root, not a bare flag.

## Tests

Loop/phase tests go in `tests/agent/`; patch the binding the phase actually reads (siblings often
`from run_agent import X` inside the function — root "patch where production reads"). Assert
message-shape invariants (alternation, byte-stable system prompt) rather than snapshotting prompt
text.

Long-form: `website/docs/developer-guide/agent-loop.md`, `prompt-assembly.md`,
`context-compression-and-caching.md`, `provider-runtime.md`, `session-storage.md`,
`subagent-lifecycle-api.md`.

## What Hermes Is

gateway (Telegram, Discord, Slack, ~20 platforms), a TUI, and an Electron desktop app. It
learns across sessions (memory + skills), delegates to subagents, runs scheduled jobs, and
drives a real terminal and browser. It is extended primarily through **plugins and skills**,
not by growing the core.

  cost. We do not do it; the ONE exception is context compression. Slash commands that mutate
  system-prompt state (skills, tools, memory) must be **cache-aware**: default to deferred
  invalidation (takes effect next session) with an opt-in `--now` flag (`/skills install --now`
  is the canonical pattern).

  CLI command + skill, a service-gated tool, or a plugin — not as core surface.

recognize design intent and *avoid wrongly closing a legitimate contribution*.

expands aggressively on purpose. The restraint below targets the **core agent + model tool
schema**, the one place where every addition is paid for on every API call. "Smallest
footprint" governs *how a capability is wired into the core*, not whether the product may
grow: expansive at the edges, conservative at the waist.

  where it manifests, and fix the whole bug class — sibling call paths included.
- **Expand reach at the edges.** New adapters, channels, providers, models, desktop/TUI/
  dashboard features land routinely, including large ones — as long as they integrate with
  the existing setup/config UX (`hermes tools`, `hermes setup`, auto-install) rather than
  bolting on a raw env var.

  wanted work. "Every line traces to the request" applies to *feature* PRs; a declared
  refactor's request IS the extraction.
- **Keep the core narrow.** Prefer, in order: extend existing code → CLI command + skill →
  service-gated tool (`check_fn`) → plugin → MCP server in the catalog → new core tool (last
  resort). See the Footprint Ladder.
- **Extend, don't duplicate.** Check whether existing infrastructure covers the use case
  before adding a module/manager/hook. When 3+ open PRs integrate the same *category*
  (memory backends, providers, notifiers), design an ABC + orchestrator, wrap the existing
  built-in as the first provider, and turn the competing PRs into plugins against it.
- **Behavior contracts over snapshots.** Tests assert how two pieces of data relate, never
  freeze a current value (see Testing).
- **E2E validation, not just green unit mocks.** Anything touching resolution chains, config
  propagation, security boundaries, remote backends, or file/network I/O must exercise the
  real path with real imports against a temp `HERMES_HOME` — two of them (A→B→A) when the
  change touches profile scope. Mocks hide integration bugs.
- **Cache-, alternation-, and invariant-safe.** Preserve prompt caching, strict role
  alternation (never two same-role messages in a row; never a synthetic user message injected
  mid-loop), and a system prompt byte-stable for the life of a conversation.
- **Contributor credit preserved.** Salvage external work by cherry-picking (rebase-merge) so
  authorship survives; build on top rather than reimplementing.

### What we don't want (rejected even when well-built)

- **Speculative infrastructure.** Hooks/callbacks/extension points with no concrete consumer.
  Adding a hook is easy; removing one after plugins depend on it is hard. A hook with a real,
  stated use case is NOT speculative even if the consumer ships separately.
- **New `HERMES_*` env vars for non-secret config.** `.env` is for secrets only. Behavioral
  settings (timeouts, thresholds, flags, display prefs) go in `config.yaml`; bridge to an
  internal env var in code if the mechanism needs one. Reject "set X in your .env" docs
  unless X is a credential.
- **A new core tool when terminal + file (or a skill) already do the job.** If the only
  barrier is file visibility on a remote backend, fix the mount, not the toolset.
- **Lazy-reading escape hatches on instructional tools.** No `offset`/`limit` pagination on
  tools that load content the agent must read fully (skills, prompts, playbooks) — models
  read page 1 and skip the rest.
- **"Fixes" that destroy the feature they secure.** Read the original intent
  (`git log -p -S`) before restricting behavior; find a fix that preserves the feature.
- **Outbound telemetry / usage attribution without opt-in gating.** No analytics,
  third-party identifier tagging, or attribution tags until a generic user-facing opt-in
  (config gate + setup prompt + `hermes tools` toggle) exists. Park behind a label.
- **Change-detector tests, cache-breaking mid-conversation, dead code wired in without E2E
  proof, plugins that touch core files.** Plugins work within the ABCs/hooks we provide; if
  one needs more, widen the generic plugin surface, never special-case it in core.
- **Third-party products integrated into the core tree.** Observability backends, vendor
  SaaS connectors, analytics dashboards, and other "someone else's product" plugins do NOT
  land under `plugins/` — every one becomes our burden against a fast-moving core for a
  backend we don't own. Ship as a **standalone plugin repo** (`~/.hermes/plugins/` or pip
  entry point), promoted in the Nous Research Discord `#plugins-skills-and-skins`. This is a
  coupling decision, not a quality bar; such PRs are closed with a pointer to publish.

### Before you call it a bug — verify the premise (and when NOT to close)

The most common reason a well-written PR is closed is a **wrong premise** or treating an
**intentional design as a gap**. These patterns tell a reviewer what to scrutinize and tell
the sweeper when a PR is NOT safe to close (when in doubt, leave it open for a human):

- **"Intentional design, not a gap."** Ask whether the isolation IS the design. Profiles are
  independent islands on purpose: a PR adding live config inheritance from the default
  profile was closed because coupling profiles is exactly what the design prevents (`--clone`
  already covers "start from my default"). Read `git log -p -S "<symbol>"` before assuming
  something is unfinished.
- **"The premise doesn't hold against how X actually works."** Trace the real runtime before
  accepting a rationale. Real closes: a rate-limit "re-probe during cooldown" PR (the breaker
  trips only on a *confirmed-empty* bucket, so re-probing hammers a bucket proven empty); a
  usage fix whose new branch **never executes** because an earlier guard already popped the
  state. If you can't point to the exact line where the bug manifests AND show the fix changes
  that line's behavior, the premise is unverified.
- **"The absence was deliberate."** Restoring "missing" `__init__.py` files made a test tree
  importable as a dotted package that shadowed the real plugin and deleted its `register()`
  at import time. The omission was load-bearing.
- **"Overreached / resurrected an approach we moved past."** Scope creep beyond the agreed
  base, or reviving a direction maintainers closed, is rejected even when it works. Offer the
  rest as a focused follow-up.

a fix.** A reproduction on current `main` plus a line-level account beats a plausible
rationale. When unsure about intent, asking is cheaper than shipping a fix that fights the
design.

### The Footprint Ladder (new capability decision)

Choose the highest (least-footprint) rung that correctly solves the problem:

1. **Extend existing code** — a variation of something that exists. Zero new surface.
2. **CLI command + skill** — config/state/infra expressible as shell commands; the agent runs
   `hermes <subcommand>` guided by a skill. Default for subscriptions, scheduled tasks,
   service setup (`hermes webhook`, `hermes cron`, `hermes tools`).
3. **Service-gated tool (`check_fn`)** — needs structured params/returns AND only appears when
   a prerequisite is configured (Home Assistant tools, memory-provider tools). This rung gates
   reachability/opt-in process-wide; a capability that varies per SESSION (who is watching) is
   a named toolset folded in by the toolset resolver, not a `check_fn` — see "Surface capability
   is a property of the SESSION" below.
4. **Plugin** — third-party/niche/user-specific; lives in `~/.hermes/plugins/` or a pip
   package, discovered at runtime.
5. **MCP server (in the catalog)** — genuinely a tool but not core-fundamental. Zero permanent
   core-schema footprint, reusable by any MCP host, reached via the built-in MCP client.
6. **New core tool** — only when fundamental, broadly useful to nearly every user, and
   unreachable via terminal + file or an MCP server (terminal, read_file, web_search,
   browser_navigate).

### Surface capability is a property of the SESSION, never of the process env

A tool that works only because of *who is on the other end* (desktop panes, in-app browser,
message reactions, Projects) must resolve availability from the **session's own source**, not
from an env var on the backend. Client and backend are separate machines: the desktop app may
drive a locally spawned backend, one over SSH, one behind URL + token, or Hermes Cloud, and
only the first two carry `HERMES_DESKTOP=1`. An env-keyed gate is a silent no-op on the other
topologies — the tool is stripped from the schema while the platform hint tells the model it
is "inside the Hermes desktop app". The pattern:

- **The toolset is the surface gate.** Keep such tools off `_HERMES_CORE_TOOLS` and in a named
  toolset (`desktop_ui`, `project`); the GUI gateway's `_load_enabled_toolsets(platform)`
  folds it in when the session's platform says GUI. One resolver, every topology.
- **`check_fn` answers reachability or opt-in, not surface.** "Is the bridge wired?" — fine.
  "Was I spawned by Electron?" — not. `check_fn` results are TTL-cached process-wide
  (`tools/registry.py`); a per-session answer does not belong there.
- **Ask which identity you mean.** `HERMES_DESKTOP=1` legitimately means "this backend was
  spawned by the app" (cron ticker, web-dist handling). It does NOT mean "a GUI is watching";
  the embedded terminal pane (`hermes --tui` against that backend) is the counterexample.

Test: if the capability still makes sense with the client on another machine, it is
session-scoped. Assert the GUI session gets the tool **with the env var absent**.

This root file holds only what applies everywhere. Each area has its own `AGENTS.md` (aim for
~8k chars; `agent/subdirectory_hints.py` delivers up to 32k and truncates head/tail with a warning
past that); see the **routing table** at the end and read the area file before editing in that area.

**Never give up on the right solution.**

## What Hermes Is

Hermes is a personal AI agent that runs the same agent core across a CLI, a messaging
gateway (Telegram, Discord, Slack, ~20 platforms), a TUI, and an Electron desktop app. It
learns across sessions (memory + skills), delegates to subagents, runs scheduled jobs, and
drives a real terminal and browser. It is extended primarily through **plugins and skills**,
not by growing the core.

Two invariants shape almost every design decision and are the lens for reviewing any change:

- **Per-conversation prompt caching is sacred.** A long-lived conversation reuses a cached
  prefix every turn. Anything that mutates past context, swaps toolsets, reloads memories, or
  rebuilds the system prompt mid-conversation invalidates that cache and multiplies the user's
  cost. We do not do it; the ONE exception is context compression. Slash commands that mutate
  system-prompt state (skills, tools, memory) must be **cache-aware**: default to deferred
  invalidation (takes effect next session) with an opt-in `--now` flag (`/skills install --now`
  is the canonical pattern).
- **The core is a narrow waist; capability lives at the edges.** Every model tool is sent on
  every API call, so the bar for a new *core* tool is high. New capability should arrive as a
  CLI command + skill, a service-gated tool, or a plugin — not as core surface.

recognize design intent and *avoid wrongly closing a legitimate contribution*.

behavior, and the product surface (platforms, providers, models, desktop/TUI features)
expands aggressively on purpose. The restraint below targets the **core agent + model tool
schema**, the one place where every addition is paid for on every API call. "Smallest
footprint" governs *how a capability is wired into the core*, not whether the product may
grow: expansive at the edges, conservative at the waist.

  dashboard features land routinely, including large ones — as long as they integrate with

  bolting on a raw env var.

  wanted work. "Every line traces to the request" applies to *feature* PRs; a declared
  refactor's request IS the extraction.

  resort). See the Footprint Ladder.

  built-in as the first provider, and turn the competing PRs into plugins against it.

  unless X is a credential.

rationale. When unsure about intent, asking is cheaper than shipping a fix that fights the

Choose the highest (least-footprint) rung that correctly solves the problem:

1. **Extend existing code** — a variation of something that exists. Zero new surface.
2. **CLI command + skill** — config/state/infra expressible as shell commands; the agent runs

3. **Service-gated tool (`check_fn`)** — needs structured params/returns AND only appears when
   a prerequisite is configured (Home Assistant tools, memory-provider tools). This rung gates

5. **MCP server (in the catalog)** — genuinely a tool but not core-fundamental. Zero permanent

+        raise AccessError('Enter valid personal details using one line per field.')

+            raise AccessError('Enter a valid email address.')

# Playwright CLI Skill

Drive a real browser from the terminal using `playwright-cli`. Prefer the bundled wrapper script so the CLI works even when it is not globally installed.
Treat this skill as CLI-first automation. Do not pivot to `@playwright/test` unless the user explicitly asks for test files.

## Prerequisite check (required)

Before proposing commands, check whether `npx` is available (the wrapper depends on it):

```bash
command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1
```

If it is not available, pause and ask the user to install Node.js/npm (which provides `npx`). Provide these steps verbatim:

```bash
# Verify Node/npm are installed
node --version
npm --version

# If missing, install Node.js/npm, then:
npm install -g @playwright/cli@latest
playwright-cli --help
```

Once `npx` is present, proceed with the wrapper script. A global install of `playwright-cli` is optional.

## Skill path (set once)

```bash
export CODEX_HOME="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}"
export PWCLI="$CODEX_HOME/skills/playwright/scripts/playwright_cli.sh"
```

User-scoped skills install under `$CODEX_HOME/skills` (default: `~/.codex/skills`).

## Quick start

Use the wrapper script:

```bash
"$PWCLI" open https://playwright.dev --headed
"$PWCLI" snapshot
"$PWCLI" click e15
"$PWCLI" type "Playwright"
"$PWCLI" press Enter
"$PWCLI" screenshot
```

If the user prefers a global install, this is also valid:

```bash
npm install -g @playwright/cli@latest
playwright-cli --help
```

## Core workflow

1. Open the page.
2. Snapshot to get stable element refs.
3. Interact using refs from the latest snapshot.
4. Re-snapshot after navigation or significant DOM changes.
5. Capture artifacts (screenshot, pdf, traces) when useful.

Minimal loop:

```bash
"$PWCLI" open https://example.com
"$PWCLI" snapshot
"$PWCLI" click e3
"$PWCLI" snapshot
```

## When to snapshot again

Snapshot again after:

- navigation
- clicking elements that change the UI substantially
- opening/closing modals or menus
- tab switches

Refs can go stale. When a command fails due to a missing ref, snapshot again.

## Recommended patterns

### Form fill and submit

```bash
"$PWCLI" open https://example.com/form
"$PWCLI" snapshot
"$PWCLI" fill e1 "user@example.com"
"$PWCLI" fill e2 "password123"
"$PWCLI" click e3
"$PWCLI" snapshot
```

### Debug a UI flow with traces

```bash
"$PWCLI" open https://example.com --headed
"$PWCLI" tracing-start
# ...interactions...
"$PWCLI" tracing-stop
```

### Multi-tab work

```bash
"$PWCLI" tab-new https://example.com
"$PWCLI" tab-list
"$PWCLI" tab-select 0
"$PWCLI" snapshot
```
