@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_private_crud_is_encrypted_durable_owner_scoped_and_csrf_protected(service):
    http=TestClient(TestServer(VaultWeb(service,service.config).app));await http.start_server()
    try:
        saved={}
        for owner,kind,fields in [('UA','phone',PHONE),('UB','email',{'email':'second@example.invalid'}),('UA','email',{'email':'first@example.invalid'}),('UA','address',ADDRESS)]:
            sid=service.store.new_session('TT',owner)
            headers={'Origin':'https://vault.example','Cookie':'__Host-clanker='+sid,'X-CSRF-Token':service.store.session(sid)['csrf']}
            response=await http.post('/api/personal/save',json={'kind':kind,'fields':fields},headers=headers)
            result=await response.json();assert response.status==200,result
            assert result['personal_info'][kind]['saved']
            assert all(value not in json.dumps(result) for value in fields.values() if len(value)>4)
            store=PersonalStore(service.private_home('TT',owner))
            assert store.values(kind)==validate(kind,fields)
            for path in (store._vault_path,service.store.path):
                assert all(value.encode() not in path.read_bytes() for value in fields.values())
            assert (store._vault_path.stat().st_mode&0o777)==0o600
            assert VaultStore(service.private_home('TT',owner)/'vault').list_items()==[]
            response=await http.post('/api/personal/details',json={'kind':kind},headers=headers)
            assert (await response.json())['fields']==validate(kind,fields)
            response=await http.post('/api/personal/details',json={'kind':kind},headers=headers|{'X-CSRF-Token':'bad'})
            assert response.status==403
            response=await http.post('/api/personal/save',json={'kind':kind,'fields':fields,'owner':'UB'},headers=headers)
            assert response.status==400
            response=await http.post('/api/personal/save',json={'kind':kind,'fields':fields},headers=headers|{'Origin':'https://evil.invalid'})
            assert response.status==403
            saved[owner]=headers
        assert PersonalStore(service.private_home('TT','UB')).values('phone') is None
        assert PersonalStore(service.private_home('TT','UB')).values('address') is None
        headers=saved['UA'];response=await http.post('/api/personal/save',json={'kind':'email','fields':{'email':'changed@example.invalid'}},headers=headers)
        assert response.status==200
        assert PersonalStore(service.private_home('TT','UA')).values('email')['email']=='changed@example.invalid'
        response=await http.post('/api/personal/remove',json={'kind':'phone'},headers=headers)
        assert response.status==200 and not (await response.json())['personal_info']['phone']['saved']
        assert PersonalStore(service.private_home('TT','UA')).values('phone') is None
        assert PersonalStore(service.private_home('TT','UB')).values('email')['email']=='second@example.invalid'
        response=await http.post('/api/personal/details',json={'kind':'email'},headers={'Origin':'https://vault.example'})
        assert response.status==401
    finally:await http.close()


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_primary_phone_is_reused_on_new_origins_but_site_accounts_win(service):
    owner_home=service.private_home('TT','UA');PersonalStore(owner_home).save('phone',PHONE)
    service.cloud_browser=SimpleNamespace(login_origin=lambda *a,**kw:'https://first.example')
    first=await service.request_access(turn(service),login_method='sms')
    assert first['status']=='access_ready' and first['origin']=='https://first.example'
    assert '+91' not in json.dumps(first) and '9876543210' not in json.dumps(first)
    again=await service.request_access(turn(service),login_method='sms')
    assert again['handle']==first['handle']
    service.cloud_browser.login_origin=lambda *a,**kw:'https://second.example'
    second=await service.request_access(turn(service),login_method='sms')
    assert second['handle']!=first['handle']
    vault=VaultStore(owner_home/'vault')
    assert vault.resolve_secret(first['handle'])==vault.resolve_secret(second['handle'])=={'phone_number':'+919876543210'}
    PersonalStore(owner_home).save('phone',{'phone_number':'+12025550101','country_code':'+1'})
    existing=await service.request_access(turn(service),login_method='sms')
    assert existing['handle']==second['handle']
    # Changing a primary never rewrites a site's selected login number.
    assert vault.resolve_secret(existing['handle'])['phone_number']=='+919876543210'
    guest=await service.request_access(turn(service,'UB'),login_method='sms')
    assert guest['status']=='waiting_for_owner'
    assert VaultStore(service.private_home('TT','UB')/'vault').list_items()==[]
    with pytest.raises(AccessError):service.delegations.invite({'team':'TT','owner':'UA'},'phone','UB')


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_private_form_defaults_use_primary_email_only_when_identifier_missing(service):
    PersonalStore(service.private_home('TT','UA')).save('email',{'email':'primary@example.invalid'})
    row=request(service);sid=service.store.new_session('TT','UA')
    headers={'Origin':'https://vault.example','Cookie':'__Host-clanker='+sid}
    http=TestClient(TestServer(VaultWeb(service,service.config).app));await http.start_server()
    try:
        data={'id':row['id'],'token':service.store.token(row['id'])}
        result=await (await http.post('/api/request',json=data,headers=headers)).json()
        assert result['defaults']=={} and result['identifier']=='owner@example.invalid'
        with service.store.connection() as db:db.execute("UPDATE requests SET identifier='' WHERE id=?",(row['id'],))
        result=await (await http.post('/api/request',json=data,headers=headers)).json()
        assert result['defaults']['email']=='primary@example.invalid'
        other=service.store.new_session('TT','UB')
        response=await http.post('/api/request',json=data,headers=headers|{'Cookie':'__Host-clanker='+other})
        assert response.status==403
    finally:await http.close()

# Phone number and SMS login

Implemented and verified locally on 6 October 2026. The running Slack gateway
has not been restarted to activate this change. Real Swiggy/Nike sign-in and
SMS delivery have not been exercised.

The original Swiggy task opened a `type=tel`, `id=mobile` login field. The
password/email-only detector rejected it twice before creating a private link.
Phone-only login now uses the existing owner-bound hosted flow in two stages:

1. Request private login access on the actual HTTPS phone login page. Local
   `auto` mode recognizes a visible phone field without a password field;
   `login_method=sms` selects it explicitly. `password` remains available for
   sites that ask for a password after a phone identifier.
2. The authenticated owner saves only their number in the private form. Numbers
   accept 7–15 digits, optional leading `+`, and ordinary formatting separators.
   The native encrypted login vault stores the number; metadata exposes only
   its final four digits and the SMS login method. No dummy password is stored.
3. Saving resumes the original task. `clanker_vault_fill` fills the number in
   the same authorized browser origin. The agent requests the website's SMS
   using the website controls.
4. `clanker_vault_enter_code` sends a private one-time code form. Submission
   resumes the same task; that tool enters the code and the agent finishes and
   verifies the website login. A subsequent login requests a fresh code.

Existing code storage remains encrypted, owner/handle/origin/task-bound,
short-lived and single use. Invited logins request SMS codes from the credential
owner. Revoked invitations cannot submit or use pending codes. Shared-channel
tasks continue through the existing isolated requester-owned private detour.

Visible fields are inspected with the native classifier. Phone detection rejects
OTP fields, hidden fields, country-code fields, extension fields and ambiguous
phone inputs. SMS codes support a single field and 4–8 adjacent one-character
boxes, including widgets without autocomplete labels. The code length must
match a split widget. Phone numbers that exceed a site's field length are
refused rather than truncated.

Both cloud adapters pass phone numbers through a separate secret binding and
keep them out of task text. Browser Tool still relies on provider-reported
origins; it cannot independently infer a phone form, so its agent must choose
`login_method=sms`. Local supervised browsing takes precedence when active.

Verification: 123 tests passed across vault, phone/SMS, both cloud adapters,
invitations, payments, channel tasks/control and native vault compatibility.
The actual Seatbelt Chromium probe ran A→B→A with two encrypted homes, private
HTTP submissions, native phone and six-box code fills, two automatic resumes,
one-use code checks and number/code output redaction. Slack delivery and the
SMS website were fixtures. Playwright verified desktop/mobile forms, failed
save preservation, retry, SMS submission and confirmation.

- [Verification receipt](../../verification/evidence/2026-10-06-phone-sms-login.json)
- [Browser acceptance](../../verification/evidence/2026-10-06-phone-login-browser.json)
- [Phone form](../../output/playwright/phone-login-form.png)
- [Mobile phone form](../../output/playwright/phone-login-mobile.png)
- [SMS form](../../output/playwright/phone-login-sms-code.png)

`patches/hermes/phone-sms-login.patch` reproduces and reverses this task's native
vault change against the preserved pre-change source. It is appended to
`scripts/apply-hermes-mods`. A full existing-stack reverse check stopped at an
unrelated pre-existing mismatch in `slack-acknowledgement.patch` against
`hermes/plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py:2274`; that code was left untouched.

No real account, SMS, purchase, Slack message or gateway restart was performed.

a masked email, the phone's final four digits and a generic address summary.
The private owner form can load full values for editing; closing it clears the
fields. Personal values are not saved in browser localStorage or sessionStorage.

## Reuse

- New local SMS sign-in requests can use the primary phone without asking for
  the number again. The handler creates a normal encrypted login bound to the
  inspected HTTPS website origin. Existing website-specific numbers take
  precedence. `use_primary=false` opens the private form for a different number.
- Private password login forms offer the primary email only when the website
  login has no saved identifier. Existing website identifiers take precedence.
- `clanker_personal_fill` resolves email, phone and address inside the requesting
  owner's supervised local browser. It checks the exact HTTPS origin, browser
  ownership, visible fields, ambiguity and field length before filling. An
  explicit national phone field or a matching nearby calling code can use the
  national part of the number. Address input, textarea and select controls are
  supported through the native classifier and fill machinery.
- Tool results report availability and fill counts without returning full
  primary values. Personal values and the filled representations are registered
  with the existing browser/terminal output redactor in private turns.
- The tool does not submit a form. Saving personal info does not authorize a
  purchase, registration or unrelated task. SMS codes remain fresh, temporary
  and single use through the existing private code flow.

Changing or removing a primary value does not rewrite or remove previously
saved website logins. This is stated in the owner form. Multiple saved accounts
on one website require deliberate account selection. Primary personal-info
fills currently require the supervised local browser; cloud adapters retain
their existing website-bound credential flows. Saving primary details in the
management page does not automatically resume a pending agent task.

## Verification

134 tests passed across personal info, vault, phone/SMS, both cloud adapters,
invitations, payments, channel tasks/control and native vault compatibility.
Python compilation and JavaScript syntax checks passed.

An actual Seatbelt Chromium probe ran A→B→A with two encrypted owner homes,
dummy contact details, owner-authenticated HTTP saves and controlled DOM forms
at two HTTPS origins. It confirmed repeated cross-site SMS, email and address
fills, national phone formatting, output redaction, wrong-origin refusal and
separate owner stores. No repeat contact form or Slack contact message was sent.
The HTTP tests also exercised CSRF, owner/origin rejection, durability, website
overrides and keeping personal entries out of invitations.

Playwright verified actual UI save, edit, remove, reload persistence, clearing
closed fields, browser-storage checks and mobile Save visibility. The verified
desktop, mobile and address-edit screenshots were added to the clanker
Lunagraph project's Page 1 and focused at Zoom to selection. They are exact
screenshots of the tested implementation, with dummy data.

- [Verification receipt](../../verification/evidence/2026-10-06-personal-info.json)
- [Chromium receipt](../../verification/evidence/2026-10-06-personal-info-browser.json)
- [Desktop](../../output/playwright/personal-info-saved.png)
- [Mobile](../../output/playwright/personal-info-mobile.png)
- [Mobile address editor](../../output/playwright/personal-info-address-mobile.png)

No real personal data was collected or saved, and no real account login, SMS,
purchase, Slack message or gateway restart was performed. The phone number in
the user's reference screenshot was not copied into the vault.

When the user asks for another version of something already on the canvas ("a variant of this screen", "the same card but dark", "duplicate this row"), **copy it with `canvas_duplicate` and edit the copy.** Never redraw it from scratch, and never `canvas_read` a big tree just to paste it back through `canvas_add` — large trees come back as `lunagraph:truncated` stubs and the copy loses whole sections.
1. `canvas_duplicate` the source id with `claim_new=true`. The copy carries every detail, gets fresh ids, and a top-level copy is parked beside the original.
2. `canvas_grep` / `canvas_query` with `root_id` set to the new id to locate only the parts that change.
3. `canvas_edit` those parts → `take_screenshot` → `canvas_release`.
Redraw from scratch only when the user asks for something genuinely new, not a variant.

## Adding New Content
When creating new elements on the canvas:
1. State a one-sentence mood/palette/type/density commitment to the user.
2. If the active page already has frames (canvas_list lists them), do **not** draw a new root on top of them. Omit x/y so the editor parks the shell to the right of existing work. To change existing work, canvas_read + claim it — do not rebuild a parallel frame on top.
3. Use canvas_add with claim_new=true for a meaningful visible shell, not a generic "Building..." placeholder and not the entire finished page/card. This adds and locks the new root in one call. The canvas paints as the JSX streams in.
4. Use the returned claim_id to add 2–4 meaningful chunks with canvas_add(parent_id) / canvas_insert so the user watches it build.
5. Take one screenshot after the complete draft, fix only material issues, then release. Do not retry a failed screenshot as separate tool calls; the tool performs one bounded internal retry for render-timing failures.

## Element IDs
- Never guess IDs — they look like "html-abc123xyz" or "el-1234567890-0".
- Use canvas_read / canvas_grep / canvas_query (or referenced-element context) to get exact IDs before canvas_claim.

## Canvas Code Rules
- `className` for Tailwind classes, `style` for inline CSS — never mix them.
- Tailwind arbitrary values (w-[800px]) don't work — use style={{ width: 800 }}.
- With no usable project theme, prefer inline CSS for reference-exact geometry, type, and color; do not discover missing utility classes through trial and error.
- No .map() on canvas (write rows explicitly). .map() is fine inside component files.
- No TanStack Table / React Hook Form — use existing components or plain HTML.

## Three.js and WebGL (SUPPORTED)
- Lunagraph supports WebGL component files, including `three`, `@react-three/fiber`, and `@react-three/drei`. When the user asks for 3D/WebGL, use it; do not replace it with CSS 3D or SVG merely because the project has no `package.json`.
- Create the scene in a `.tsx` component with `project_write`, then place that component on the canvas. Direct Three.js (for example `import * as THREE from 'three'`) and React Three Fiber are both valid.
- For browser rendering, bare npm imports are rewritten to esm.sh even when they are not declared in the user's project `package.json`; a declaration pins the requested version. The builder separately maintains an internal install manifest and may auto-install packages for prop scanning/CSS tooling, so the AI does not need to perform or invent a manual dependency-install step.
- Lunagraph automatically preserves WebGL drawing buffers so `take_screenshot` can capture the scene. Verify the result with `take_screenshot`; if capture fails, report the actual tool error instead of assuming WebGL or the import is unsupported.
- WebGL scenes are file-edited rather than converted into editable DOM layers. This does not limit rendering, canvas placement, props, or screenshots.

## Component Workflow (creating new components)
- Use project_write to create component files in components/ directory (e.g. components/Modal.tsx, components/ui/Card.tsx).
- A component MUST exist as a file before it can be used on canvas — otherwise "Component not found".
- **Never reserve a name with a stub.** Do not write a green/red/empty placeholder so the component "registers." Copy or write the real file (and every file it imports) first, then put it on the canvas. A stub that imports missing CSS crashes as a red box and is worse than waiting.
- For full pages: Create 3-5 small component files, then compose on canvas with canvas_add.
- **Keep internal helper components stateless.** Sub-components in the same file should NOT use useState/useEffect — pass state down as props, or split into their own files.
- **Color props**: name them with a `color`/`Color`/`bg`/`Background`/`fill`/`stroke`/`tint`/`accent` suffix (e.g. `backgroundColor`, `accentColor`, `fillColor`) AND give them a CSS color literal default like `'#3b82f6'`, `'rgb(...)'`, or `'oklch(...)'` — never a theme-token name like `'primary'`. This makes Lunagraph render a color picker in the props panel.
- **Flat props, not nested objects.** Lunagraph's props panel can only edit primitive props (string, number, boolean, enum string union). `title: string` ✓, `size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` ✓, `disabled: boolean` ✓. `config: { variant: string; size: number }` ✗ — the user can't edit nested values in the panel. If you need related props, FLATTEN them: `configVariant` + `configSize` rather than a nested `config` object. Same goes for arrays of objects (`items: Item[]`) — those become opaque blobs in the panel; better to either accept them as required-props-with-mocks (for table-like components that genuinely need a list) or expose individual props per item if the count is small + fixed.
- **Required vs optional props.** Mark optional props with `?` and provide sensible defaults — Lunagraph uses these defaults when the user drops the component on canvas without configuring anything. Required props with no defaults force the user to configure before they see anything render.

## Lunagraph internals — where things live

Quick reference for ad-hoc questions about the project's settings/state:

- **Tailwind tokens** → `tailwind.config.*` + `app/globals.css` (`@theme inline` / `:root { --token }` blocks). Cloud's css-builder picks up changes automatically on file write.
- **Fonts** → declared self-contained in `app/globals.css`: an `@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/...')` for Google families plus literal family names in the `@theme inline` block (`--font-sans` / `--font-serif` / `--font-mono`, e.g. `--font-serif: 'Domine', serif`). The css-builder extracts the `@import` URL and injects it as a `<link>`; the literal `@theme` tokens compile straight into `font-*` utilities. No separate settings file, no `var()` indirection.
- **Icon library preference** → `project.settings.iconLibraries` JSONB column on the project row. Auto-detected from likely icon packages in `package.json` deps if not set explicitly. To change it during an import, use the `set_icon_library` MCP tool with any npm package that exports named React icon components.
- **Allowed local paths** → per-project, set via Settings UI in the editor. Listed in session context when connected from Lunagraph chat.
- **Canvas pages** → `page` table (one row per canvas tab). Use `canvas_list` to see them; the project always has at least one canvas.
- **Project files** → `file` table, accessed via `project_read`/`project_write`/`project_glob`/`project_grep` MCP tools. Path-based, like a regular filesystem.
- **Lunagraph skills** → app-owned workflow recipes exposed through `list_skills` and `read_skill` MCP tools. They are not Claude-global skills and should be fetched from Lunagraph when needed.
- **Component scan results** → `project.scanResult` JSONB. Cached. Use `search_components` MCP tool to query rather than reading directly.

If the user asks "where is X stored?" or "how do I change Y?" — answer from this reference. If a setting needs a tool that doesn't exist yet, say so honestly and offer the workaround.

Other skills (e.g. `lunagraph-import-from-project`) load on demand when that workflow applies.
- If the user names an exact skill, call read_skill with that exact name directly. Do not call list_skills first.

## Porting Local Components to Lunagraph
When copying a component from the user's local codebase into the Lunagraph project:
1. Copy the **real** source with `project_copy_file` (or `files[]` for the component plus every local import it needs — CSS modules, icons, helpers). Do **not** `local_read` + `project_write` the same bytes. Do **not** write a colored placeholder / stub first to "register the name." Images/fonts still use `project_copy_asset`.
2. `project_edit` only the lines that must change for Lunagraph:
   - **Strip server-side code**: Remove API calls, DB queries, `'use server'`, auth checks → replace with realistic mock data
   - **Fix imports**: Change local repo import paths to Lunagraph project paths (`@/components/...`)

   - **Type your props**: Use TypeScript interfaces so Lunagraph can extract prop info

   - CSS-in-JS (styled-components, emotion) doesn't work — use Tailwind or CSS files

# Designing on the Lunagraph canvas

You are acting as a senior product designer, not a code generator. Work should look
*intentionally designed*: clear hierarchy, considered spacing, real content, and an
obvious primary action. Looking "nice" without a clear job still fails.

## PRIME DIRECTIVE — derive the language, don't impose one

There is no single "Lunagraph look." Taste here is a **method**, not a fixed aesthetic.
Every design must feel like it belongs to *this* project. You never start from your own
default style. You first read what the project already is, then design within it.

The craft rules below are universal (they are about relationships: contrast, rhythm,
alignment). Every concrete value (the accent color, the radius, the spacing unit, how
loud the palette is, whether shadows exist) comes from the project, not from you.

## PRIME DIRECTIVE 2 — design in nouns before you write tags

A human designer thinks "I want a warning badge, a secondary button, and a primary
button." They do not think "I am writing a span." You must work the same way, because
naming the noun is what makes you reach for the existing component.

**Before any JSX for a region, write one line naming every element as a design noun.**
Not tags. Nouns: badge, primary button, secondary button, card, input, avatar, tooltip,
table row, banner, tab, empty state, divider, icon button, checkbox.

Then resolve every noun to a real component before typing `<`.

This is the single highest-value habit in this skill. The most common failure mode is
not ignorance of the rule; it is emitting JSX left to right and only noticing afterwards
that the `<span>` you wrote was a badge all along. Naming it first prevents that.

## Scope beats polish on edits

When the user @-mentions an existing element and asks for a **delta** (add a column,
change a label, insert a row): **only change what they asked for.** Adjacent cells,
categories, status badges, and padding stay byte-identical. Prefer `canvas_grep` /
`canvas_query` then `canvas_edit` / `canvas_insert` over `canvas_update`. Do not rebuild
a parallel frame. If you want to improve something adjacent, say so in text and wait for
the user to ask.

## Variations start from a copy, never from a redraw

"Make a variant of this screen with a different right sidebar", "the same card in dark",
"another row like that one" — the answer is `canvas_duplicate` on the source id, then a
surgical edit of the copy. Redrawing loses details the user never asked you to change,
and re-sending a read tree through `canvas_add` is worse: anything past the read budget
comes back as `{/* lunagraph:truncated … */}` stubs, so the copy silently loses sections.

1. `canvas_duplicate` the source with `claim_new: true`. A top-level copy lands in the
   nearest free slot beside the original (to its right, else below it); the copy gets
   fresh ids throughout.
2. `canvas_grep` / `canvas_query` with `root_id` set to the new id to find the parts that
   differ. The source's ids do not exist in the copy.
3. `canvas_edit` only those parts, then screenshot and release.

Everything in **Scope beats polish on edits** applies to the copy: the parts the user did
not ask about stay byte-identical to the original.

## The loop (mandatory — do not skip Name or Screenshot)

Every design task runs this loop. The visual commitment, noun list, and final screenshot
are the most commonly skipped parts and the ones that cause the most rework.

1. **Gather** — call `get_design_context` once unless the prompt already contains a
   sufficient theme, component manifest, and active-page summary. Do not separately call
   `get_theme`, `search_components`, and `canvas_list` after this combined call. The one
   exception: if you write or change the project's CSS entry during the task, its earlier
   theme result is stale — call `get_theme` again before styling anything else, or you
   will keep designing around tokens you have since created.
2. **Commit** — before mutation, tell the user the intended mood, palette, type, and
   density in one short sentence. This is a design commitment, not a request for approval.
3. **Name** — for the region you are about to build, list its parts as design nouns in
   one line. "Banner: status badge, one line of copy, secondary Learn more button,
   primary Reconnect button."
4. **Resolve** — map each noun to a component + variant from the manifest. If a noun has
   no match, `search_components` for it *now* rather than hand-rolling. Only after every
   noun is resolved (or confirmed absent) do you write JSX.
5. **Draft visibly** — for new work, add a meaningful shell with `claim_new: true`, then
   add 2–4 visible chunks using the returned claim. If the page already has frames, pass
   `anchor_id` (the user's selection, an @-referenced element, or the frame this work
   belongs with) and omit `x`/`y`, so the shell lands beside that frame rather than at the
   far edge of the canvas — never stack a new root on existing work. To change what is
   already there, `canvas_read` + claim it. The canvas
   paints as JSX streams in; still send those chunks so the user sees structure before
   details. Never leave the canvas empty while composing a full-page/full-card JSX payload.
   For edits: surgical tools only.
6. **Screenshot** — `take_screenshot` on what you built or changed. Actually look at it.
   (`canvas_release` errors if you mutated under a claim without a verifying screenshot.)
7. **Critique** — grade against the Checklist. Name only actual problems; do not force
   three changes when the screenshot already passes.
8. **Fix** — fix the material problems, then re-screenshot only if pixels changed.

Do not tell the user "done" until a screenshot has passed the Checklist.

**The loop is per region, not per task.** On a long task with several regions, run
Name → Resolve again for each one. Component knowledge gathered at minute one does not
survive to minute forty; re-stating the nouns is cheap and re-anchors you.

## Modify-existing path (user @-mentioned an element)

1. State the exact change list in thinking ("add Attachment `<th>` after Category; add
   one `<td>` per body row").
2. Use the auto-attached reference screenshot when present; otherwise `take_screenshot`
   the referenced id.
3. `canvas_grep` / `canvas_query` for anchors (`Category`, `tbody tr`). Do **not** reload
   a 100k-char root unless necessary.
4. Run **Name → Resolve** for anything new you are introducing. Surgical edits are the
   most dangerous place to skip this: you are pattern-matching on the surrounding markup,
   and if the surrounding markup is hand-rolled you will copy its mistakes. Local
   consistency is not a justification for a hand-rolled component. If neighboring code
   uses a fake badge, still use `Badge`, and mention the inconsistency to the user.
5. `canvas_read` the smallest sensible root (often the table) — required before claim. Oversized trees may include `{/* lunagraph:truncated … */}` stubs; drill those ids with another `canvas_read` when needed.
6. `canvas_claim` that same root (or a descendant). Claim returns `claim_id` (locks expire after 5 minutes — re-claim if still editing). If the parent claim isn’t needed, release and claim a smaller subset.
7. `canvas_insert` / `canvas_edit` per change. Echo `data-element-id` only on `canvas_update`.
8. `take_screenshot` the claimed element, then `canvas_release`.

## Step 1 — Derive the project's visual language

Call `get_design_context` once. It combines theme, registered components, and active-page
information. Use targeted calls only when its result says more detail is needed, or after
you write the project's CSS entry — a theme reported as missing before you created it is
not a licence to invent an inline-style system. Not everything on the canvas is canon;
users leave experiments and alternate iterations.

1. **Tokens** — use the returned theme (or Project Theme already in context). Prefer theme
   Tailwind classes (`bg-primary`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-border`) over
   hardcoded colors.
2. **User-pointed references** — if the user @-mentions elements, those are the thing to
   edit and preserve, not merely style inspiration. Match that system.
3. **Components** — use the returned component list. Call `search_components` only for a
   specific unresolved noun, not to repeat the full listing.
4. **Rest of canvas (last, optional)** — only if you still need density and spacing cues.
   Sample one or two elements.

### Write the component manifest

After the combined context call, write a short list into your reasoning, mapping **design nouns
to real components and their variants**:
badge -> Badge (variant: default | secondary | outline | warning | destructive)
button -> Button (variant: default | secondary | outline | ghost | destructive; size: sm | default | lg)
text input -> Input
container -> Card

This list is what you consult in the Resolve step. A raw list of 61 component names is
not usable mid-build; a noun-to-component map is.

**Empty project?** Establish a minimal system first: ONE neutral scale, ONE accent,
Tailwind's spacing scale, one radius, one type ramp, held consistently. Only invent raw
controls when `search_components` shows nothing suitable.

For an empty project or a precise reference replica with no usable theme, prefer inline
CSS for geometry, typography, and exact colors. This avoids relying on utility classes
that may not exist in the project's Tailwind build. When a real project theme exists,
use its Tailwind utilities so the design inherits future token changes.

## Semantics: say what a thing *is*, not what it should look like

Using the right component is half the job. Using the right **variant** is the other half.
A secondary action must carry the secondary variant, not primary styling with the visual
weight dialed down by hand.

- A secondary button is `<Button variant="secondary">`. Not a `default` Button with muted
  classes. Not `variant="outline"` chosen because it looked calmer in the screenshot.
- A cautionary status is `<Badge variant="warning">`. Not a neutral Badge with amber
  classes bolted on.
- A destructive action is `variant="destructive"`, not red text.

Two reasons this matters beyond pixels. First, the design communicates intent to the
developer who implements it; a hand-toned primary button tells them nothing about
hierarchy. Second, variants stay correct when the theme changes, and hand-picked colors
silently rot.

**Never override a component's own color, border, radius, or font-weight via `className`.**
That is a signal you picked the wrong variant. `className` on a project component is for
layout only: `w-full`, `flex-1`, `mt-2`, `shrink-0`. If no variant fits, say so to the
user rather than quietly styling around it.

## Copy rules

Design copy is part of the design. Apply these to every string you write on the canvas.

**Punctuation:**
- **No em dashes (—) in UI copy.** Use a period, a comma, or two sentences. Em dashes are
  a strong tell of machine-written text and they read as filler in dense UI. This applies
  to titles, body copy, badges, tooltips, and empty states.
- No en dashes except in genuine numeric ranges ("30–90 days").
- Prefer short sentences over one long clause-chained sentence.

**Substance:**
- Write labels a user would say out loud. "Reconnect", not "Update credentials".
  "Importing paused", not "Sync state: degraded". If a label needs the surrounding
  paragraph to make sense, the label is wrong.
- A notice must answer three questions in this order, and the user must get all three
  without reading a paragraph: what happened, what it means for me, what do I do now.
- Do not make routine states look like failures. Expected conditions (an expired token, a
  pending invite, an empty list) are calm and informational. Reserve red, warning
  triangles, and alarm language for genuine errors the user caused or must repair.
- The action in the button must obviously be the action described in the copy. If the
  notice says "Sign in again", the button says "Sign in", not something adjacent.
- Push long explanation into a tooltip, a "Learn more" affordance, or a details panel.
  The default view stays scannable.
- Realistic mock data, always. Never "Lorem ipsum", never an empty table or list.

## The Checklist (this is also the rubric)

Grade every screenshot **and the JSX** against these. Each is checkable, no vibes
required. Most "AI design" fails on spacing, hierarchy, skipping project components, and
ignoring the project's own language.

**Components and semantics**
- [ ] Every part of the region was named as a design noun before JSX was written.
- [ ] Project components used wherever they exist (`Button`, `Badge`, `Input`, …). A raw
      `<button>` or a `<span>` styled to look like a badge is a fail. Check the JSX, not
      only the screenshot. (Writes reject raw form controls when project components exist.)
- [ ] Variants carry meaning: secondary actions use the secondary variant, warnings use
      the warning variant, destructive uses destructive.
- [ ] No `className` on a project component overriding its color, border, radius, or
      weight. Layout utilities only.

**Copy**
- [ ] No em dashes anywhere in the copy.
- [ ] Every label is self-explanatory out of context.
- [ ] Non-error states do not look like errors.

**Scale and layout**
- [ ] Spacing and type come from the Tailwind scale (`p-4`, `gap-6`, `text-sm`), not
      one-off px. Theme tokens for color.
- [ ] Sibling spacing via flex/grid `gap`, not stacked margins.
- [ ] Generous whitespace. Cramped is the number one tell. When unsure, add room.

**Hierarchy**
- [ ] One clear focal point; the primary action or outcome is obvious at a glance.
- [ ] Emphasis via **size + weight + color**, not bold alone. Secondary text muted
      (`text-muted-foreground`), not a guessed gray.
- [ ] No more than about 2 to 3 type sizes in one view. Long body text left-aligned with
      a set line-height.

**Color and surface**
- [ ] Color follows the **project's** strategy. Theme tokens, not hardcoded `bg-white` or
      `text-gray-900`.
- [ ] Text meets contrast (roughly AA). Muted is not illegible.
- [ ] Elevation, borders, and radius match the project's language.

**Icons**
- [ ] `search_icons` before styling icons.
- [ ] One size source only: the `size` prop. Never `size={24}` together with `size-7`,
      `w-*`, or `h-*` on the same icon.
- [ ] On canvas: `<i data-icon="…" data-icon-library="…" size={24} className="text-muted-foreground" />`,
      with `className` for color only.

## Lunagraph canvas constraints (don't fight these)

- **Prefer Tailwind utility classes** for layout, spacing, color, type. Inline `style`
  only for values off the scale.
- `className` **or** `style`, never both on one element.
- Arbitrary Tailwind values (`w-[800px]`) do not render. Use `style={{ width: 800 }}`.
- **Icons on canvas** always need `data-icon` + `data-icon-library` + `size={N}`.
- No `.map()` on the canvas. Write rows explicitly.
- A component must exist as a file (`project_write`) before it renders on canvas.
- Prefer `canvas_edit` / `canvas_insert` over a full `canvas_update`. On update, you may
  echo `data-element-id` to preserve identity.

## Working on smaller or older models

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Invoke the project-versioned Hermes source with dedicated local state.
# The gateway is trusted; enabled generated-code tools use the Seatbelt provider.
set -euo pipefail
umask 077

project_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
lab_dir="$project_dir/.local/hermes-lab"
source_dir="$project_dir/hermes"

if [[ ! -x "$lab_dir/venv/bin/hermes" ]]; then
  echo "Install the pinned baseline first; see verification/LOCAL_BASELINE.md." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [[ ! -f "$source_dir/pyproject.toml" ]]; then
  echo "Hermes source is missing; expected hermes/ at the project root." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [[ -e "$source_dir/.env" ]]; then
  echo "The Hermes source has a fallback .env; keep credentials only in the lab home." >&2
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$lab_dir/home" "$lab_dir/workspace" "$lab_dir/gateway-locks" "$lab_dir/managed"
if [[ ! -f "$lab_dir/home/config.yaml" ]]; then
  cp "$project_dir/verification/hermes/config.yaml" "$lab_dir/home/config.yaml"
fi
if [[ ! -f "$lab_dir/home/.env" ]]; then
  touch "$lab_dir/home/.env"
fi
chmod 600 "$lab_dir/home/.env"
if [[ -f "$lab_dir/home/.clanker-execution/fleet.json" ]]; then
  if ! env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="/usr/bin:/bin" \
      "$lab_dir/venv/bin/python" "$project_dir/runtime/seatbelt/recover.py" "$lab_dir/home"; then
    echo "Browser execution is unavailable; continuing with Slack chat." >&2
  fi
fi

cd "$lab_dir/workspace"
# Credentials must be deliberately configured in the lab home. Keep HOME
# unchanged for platform compatibility; do not inherit provider/session vars.
# Command smoke: skip startup model/tool warmup until inference is configured.
exec env -i \
  HOME="$HOME" \
  PATH="$lab_dir/venv/bin:$lab_dir/home/node/bin:$lab_dir/home/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin" \
  TERM="${TERM:-xterm-256color}" \
  LANG="${LANG:-en_US.UTF-8}" \
  HERMES_HOME="$lab_dir/home" \
  PYTHONPATH="$project_dir/runtime" \
  HERMES_MANAGED_DIR="$lab_dir/managed" \
  HERMES_GATEWAY_LOCK_DIR="$lab_dir/gateway-locks" \
  HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS=1 \
  HERMES_STARTUP_WARMUP_TIMEOUT=0 \
  "$lab_dir/venv/bin/hermes" "$@"

"""Authenticated Slack turns -> private links -> durable save -> scoped resume.

The model never selects an owner, profile path, or link token. Only the live
gateway turn may bind a tool call to the already authenticated Slack source.
"""
import asyncio
from dataclasses import dataclass
import json
from pathlib import Path
import threading
from urllib.parse import urlencode, urlsplit

from .store import AccessError, RequestStore

_lock = threading.RLock()


@dataclass
class Binding:
    service: object
    source: object
    task_id: str
    message: str
    home: Path
    message_id: str = None


def binding(task_id):
    from hermes_constants import get_hermes_home
    from agent.gateway_context import current_gateway_turn
    from gateway.slack_workspace import workspace_policy
    current=current_gateway_turn()
    if current and current.task_id==str(task_id) and current.home==str(get_hermes_home()):
        policy=workspace_policy(current.runner,current.source)
        service=getattr(policy,'vault_service',None)
        if service:
            result=Binding(service,current.source,current.task_id,current.message,Path(current.home),current.message_id)
            service.validate_member(result.source.scope_id,result.source.user_id)
            if policy.authorize_source(result.source):return result
        raise AccessError('Secure access is unavailable in this session. The hosted vault must be connected by the operator.',503)
    raise AccessError('Secure access is unavailable in this session. The hosted vault must be connected by the operator.',503)


async def on_gateway_control(command, source, runner):
    if command not in ('stop','new','reset'):return None
    from gateway.slack_workspace import workspace_policy
    policy=workspace_policy(runner,source)
    service=getattr(policy,'vault_service',None)
    if service and policy.authorize_source(source):
        rows=service.store.channel_tasks_for_control(source.scope_id,source.user_id,source.to_dict())
        count=await asyncio.to_thread(service.store.cancel,team=source.scope_id,owner=source.user_id,source=source.to_dict())
        cleanup_pending=await service.channel_control.stop_sources(rows)
        conversation = policy.state['conversations'].get(source.chat_id,{})
        if (service.cloud_browser is not None and getattr(source,'isolated_task',None) is None and
                conversation.get('kind')=='dm'):
            home=policy.home if source.profile=='default' else policy.home/'profiles'/source.profile
            turn=Binding(service,source,'control','',home.resolve(strict=True))
            try:
                await asyncio.to_thread(service.cloud_browser.stop,turn)
            except Exception:
                cleanup_pending=True
        return {'cancelled_pending':count,'cleanup_pending':cleanup_pending}


class VaultService:
    def __init__(self, policy, config):
        self.policy, self.config = policy, config
        self.store = RequestStore(policy.home/'.clanker-vault')
        from .delegation import Delegations
        self.delegations = Delegations(self)
        from .personal import PersonalInfo
        self.personal = PersonalInfo(self)
        from .payments import Payments
        self.payments = Payments(self)
        self.loop = None
        self.fill_locks = {}
        self.resume_tasks = {}
        from .channel_tasks import ChannelTasks
        self.channel_tasks = ChannelTasks(self)
        from .channel_control import ChannelControl
        self.channel_control = ChannelControl(self)
        from cloud_browser.service import configured
        self.cloud_browser = configured(self)

    def validate_member(self, team, owner):
        member = self.policy.state['members'].get(owner,{})
        if team!=self.policy.team or member.get('status')!='ready':
            raise AccessError('This Slack account is not authorized for Clanker.',403)
        return member

    def private_home(self, team, owner):
        member = self.validate_member(team,owner)
        profile = member['profile']
        home = self.policy.home if profile=='default' else self.policy.home/'profiles'/profile
        home = home.resolve(strict=True)
        if home!=self.policy.home.resolve() and not home.is_relative_to((self.policy.home/'profiles').resolve()):
            raise AccessError('The private account context is unavailable.',403)
        return home

    def assert_private(self, turn):
        member = self.validate_member(turn.source.scope_id,turn.source.user_id)
        home = self.private_home(turn.source.scope_id,turn.source.user_id)
        conversation = self.policy.state['conversations'].get(turn.source.chat_id,{})
        profile = member['profile']
        if getattr(turn.source,'isolated_task',None) is not None:
            profile = self.channel_tasks.execution_route(turn.source)
            home = self.policy.home / 'profiles' / profile
        if (conversation.get('kind')!='dm' or home!=turn.home.resolve() or
                turn.source.chat_id!=member['dm_id'] or turn.source.profile!=profile or
                not self.policy.authorize_source(turn.source)):
            raise AccessError('Private accounts are available only in your DM with Clanker.',403)
        return home

    async def invitation_members(self, identity):
        self.validate_member(identity['team'], identity['owner'])
        members = []
        client = self.policy.client()
        for uid, member in self.policy.state['members'].items():
            if uid == identity['owner'] or member.get('status') != 'ready':
                continue
            label = member.get('name') or uid
            if hasattr(client, 'users_info'):
                try:
                    user = (await client.users_info(user=uid))['user']
                    label = user.get('profile', {}).get('display_name') or user.get('real_name') or user.get('name') or uid
                except Exception:
                    pass
            members.append({'id': uid, 'name': label})
        return members

    async def revoke_invitation(self, identity, grant_id):
        grant = self.delegations.revoke(identity, grant_id)
        with self.store.connection() as db:
            usages = [dict(row) for row in db.execute(
                'SELECT * FROM credential_grant_usage WHERE grant_id=? AND team=? AND recipient=?',
                (grant_id, grant['team'], grant['recipient']))]
        pending = False
        for usage in usages:
            try:
                await self.channel_control.stop_usage(usage)
            except Exception:
                # Each uncertain context retains its own usage marker. Continue
                # interrupting the other contexts that used this invitation.
                pending = True
        return {'revoked': True, 'cleanup_pending': pending}

    async def set_invitation_access(self, identity, recipient, handles):
        result = await asyncio.to_thread(self.delegations.set_access, identity, recipient, handles)
        pending = False
        # Every revoked grant can have distinct guest task cookie contexts.
        for grant_id in result['revoked']:
            with self.store.connection() as db:
                used = db.execute('SELECT 1 FROM credential_grant_usage WHERE grant_id=?', (grant_id,)).fetchone()
            if used:
                pending = (await self.revoke_invitation(identity, grant_id))['cleanup_pending'] or pending
        return {'saved': True, 'recipient': recipient, 'cleanup_pending': pending,
                'grants': [{'id': row['id'], 'handle': row['handle']} for row in result['grants']]}

    def clear_invited_browsers(self, turn):
        import shutil
        home = self.channel_control.validate_cleanup(turn)
        with self.lock_for(home):
            errors = []
            if self.cloud_browser is not None:
                try:
                    self.cloud_browser.stop(turn, purge=True)
                except Exception as error:
                    errors.append(error)
            try:
                local_errors = []
                manifest = home / '.clanker-execution' / 'context.json'
                if manifest.exists():
                    from seatbelt.context import Context
                    from seatbelt.launcher import stop_chrome
                    context = Context(home)
                    for state in (home / '.clanker-execution').glob('chrome-*.json'):
                        try:
                            stop_chrome(context, json.loads(state.read_text())['name'])
                        except Exception as error:
                            errors.append(error)
                            local_errors.append(error)
                    profile = context.browser / 'chromium'
                    if profile.exists() and not local_errors:
                        shutil.rmtree(profile)
                elif list((home / '.clanker-execution').glob('chrome-*.json')) or (home / 'browser' / 'sandbox' / 'chromium').exists():
                    raise AccessError('The local browser cleanup has no verified execution context.', 409)
            except Exception as error:
                errors.append(error)
            if errors:
                raise AccessError('Browser cleanup is still pending. This account context remains blocked.', 409)
            # Keep cleanup and its completion marker inside the guest lock.
            # A new fill must not race between cookie removal and this delete.
            with self.store.connection() as db:
                db.execute('DELETE FROM credential_grant_usage WHERE team=? AND recipient=? AND home=?',
                           (turn.source.scope_id, turn.source.user_id, str(home)))

    def call(self, coroutine):
        if self.loop is None or not self.loop.is_running():
            coroutine.close()
            raise AccessError('The hosted credential service is unavailable.',503)
        future = asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(coroutine,self.loop)
        try:
            return future.result(timeout=30)
        except TimeoutError:
            future.cancel()
            raise AccessError('The access request is still pending. Please retry shortly.',503) from None

    def lock_for(self, home):
        with _lock:
            return self.fill_locks.setdefault(str(home),threading.RLock())

    async def move_private(self, turn):
        policy = self.policy
        if (policy.state['conversations'].get(turn.source.chat_id,{}).get('kind')!='shared' or
                not policy.authorize_source(turn.source)):
            raise AccessError('This account task is not authorized in this conversation.',403)
        original = turn.source.to_dict()
        if turn.message_id:original['message_id']=turn.message_id
        edits = getattr(policy.adapter, '_message_edits', None)
        revision = edits.lookup((turn.source.scope_id, turn.source.chat_id, turn.source.user_id,
                                 original.get('message_id'))) if edits else None
        if revision:
            original['slack_request_version'] = str(revision.version)
            original['slack_request_digest'] = revision.digest
        original['thread_id'] = turn.source.thread_id or turn.source.message_id or turn.message_id
        if not original['thread_id']:
            raise AccessError('The originating Slack message is unavailable.',409)
        home=self.private_home(turn.source.scope_id,turn.source.user_id)
        row=self.store.transfer(team=turn.source.scope_id,owner=turn.source.user_id,home=home,
            task_id=turn.task_id,source=original,task=turn.message,reply_mode='channel')
        await self.deliver_transfer(row)
        await self.drain()
        return {'status':'moved_to_private','private_results':False,
                'next':'Account access is handled privately. This task will continue automatically and reply in this thread. End this turn.'}

    async def deliver_transfer(self, row):
        from gateway.session import SessionSource
        from gateway.config import Platform
        if row.get('source') or row['status']!='waiting':return
        member = self.validate_member(row['team'],row.get('approver') or row['owner'])

        if not hmac.compare_digest(str(claims['nonce']),nonce):
            raise ValueError('nonce')
        identity={'team':claims['https://slack.com/team_id'],'owner':claims['https://slack.com/user_id']}
        if not all(isinstance(value,str) and value for value in identity.values()):
            raise ValueError('identity')

        sid = self.store.new_session(identity['team'],identity['owner'])

        if row['kind']=='login':

        label=await asyncio.to_thread(self.service.approve_payment,data['id'],data['token'],identity,data['fields'])

        members = await self.service.invitation_members(identity)
        items = await asyncio.to_thread(self.service.delegations.items,identity['team'],identity['owner'])
        credentials = [item for item in items if item.get('access') != 'invited' and item['kind'] in ('login','api_key','payment')]
        return web.json_response({'invitations':invitations,'members':members,'credentials':credentials,'csrf':identity['csrf']})

        return web.json_response(await self.service.set_invitation_access(identity,data['recipient'],data['handles']))

        identity = self.identity(request,csrf=True)
        data = await request.json()
        if not isinstance(data,dict) or set(data)!={'id'}:
            raise AccessError('Choose an invitation to revoke.')
        return web.json_response(await self.service.revoke_invitation(identity,data['id']))

    async def code(self, request):
        identity=self.identity(request,csrf=True)
        data=await request.json()
        return_url=self.return_slack_url(identity)
        label=await asyncio.to_thread(self.service.save_code,data['id'],data['token'],identity,data['fields'])
        return web.json_response({'saved':True,'label':label,'return_slack_url':return_url})

    async def disconnect(self, request):
        identity = self.identity(request,csrf=True)
        data = await request.json()
        await self.service.disconnect(identity['team'],identity['owner'],data['handle'])
        return web.json_response({'removed':True})

    async def start(self):
        self.runner = web.AppRunner(self.app,access_log=None)
        await self.runner.setup()
        await web.TCPSite(self.runner,'127.0.0.1',int(self.config.get('port',8767))).start()

    async def close(self):
        await self.runner.cleanup()

        profile = member['profile']
        if row['reply_mode']=='channel':
            profile = await self.channel_tasks.prepare(row)
        message_id = 'clanker-private-'+row['id']
        from uuid import uuid5, NAMESPACE_URL
        client_id = str(uuid5(NAMESPACE_URL,message_id))
        history = await self.policy.client().conversations_history(channel=dm,limit=100)
        existing = next((m for m in history.get('messages',[]) if m.get('client_msg_id')==client_id),None)
        delivered = existing or await self.policy.client().chat_postMessage(channel=dm,
            text=("I'll collect account access privately here and return the requested result to the original thread."
                  if row['reply_mode']=='channel' else "I'll handle your account access and results privately here."),client_msg_id=client_id)
        original=json.loads(row['original_source'])
        source = SessionSource(platform=Platform.SLACK,chat_id=dm,chat_type='dm',user_id=row['owner'],
                               user_name=original.get('user_name'),thread_id=delivered['ts'],scope_id=row['team'],
                               profile=profile)
        self.store.set_transfer_source(row['id'],source.to_dict())

    async def request_access(self, turn, *, label='', identifier='', kind='login', origin='', login_method='auto', use_primary=True):
        if not isinstance(use_primary, bool):raise AccessError('Choose whether to use your primary details.')
        if login_method not in ('auto', 'password', 'sms'):
            raise AccessError('Choose a password or SMS login method.')
        try:
            home = self.assert_private(turn)
        except AccessError:
            return await self.move_private(turn)
        if kind=='api_key':
            if login_method != 'auto':raise AccessError('API key requests do not use a login method.')
            request=self.store.create(team=turn.source.scope_id,owner=turn.source.user_id,
                home=self.private_home(turn.source.scope_id,turn.source.user_id),
                task_id=turn.task_id,source=turn.source.to_dict(),task=turn.message,
                kind=kind,label=label,origin=origin,identifier=identifier,gateway_event_id=turn.message_id)
            await self.deliver_link(request)
            return {'status':'waiting_for_owner','request_id':request['id'],
                    'next':'The private API key form has been sent. End this turn. Saving the key resumes this task automatically.'}
        if kind!='login' or origin:
            raise AccessError('Login access must be bound to the actual browser login page.')
        from tools.browser_vault_tool import _current_page_origin, _ensure_supervisor
        # Origin comes from the live browser, never the model's site string.
        from .payments import local_supervisor
        if self.cloud_browser is not None and local_supervisor(turn.task_id) is None:
            options = {'phone': True} if login_method=='sms' else {}
            origin = await asyncio.to_thread(self.cloud_browser.login_origin,turn,**options)
            # URL-only providers cannot infer a form's method. The agent selects
            # sms explicitly from the provider's login-page observations.
            if login_method == 'auto':login_method = 'password'
        else:
            from gateway.run import _profile_runtime_scope
            from .login import LOGIN_FIELDS, PHONE_FIELDS, PASSWORD_FIELDS
            def login_origin():
                from seatbelt.context import Context
                supervisor=_ensure_supervisor(turn.task_id)
                if supervisor is None:raise AccessError('Open the account login page before requesting access.',409)
                Context(home).owned_cdp(supervisor.cdp_url)
                probe = PHONE_FIELDS if login_method == 'sms' else LOGIN_FIELDS
                focused=supervisor.focus_page('',accept=probe)
                if not focused.get('ok'):raise AccessError('Open the account login form before requesting access.',409)
                method = login_method
                if method == 'auto':
                    observed = supervisor.evaluate_runtime('(' + PHONE_FIELDS + ') && !(' + PASSWORD_FIELDS + ')')
                    if not observed.get('ok'):raise AccessError('Could not inspect the account login method.',409)
                    method = 'sms' if observed.get('result') is True else 'password'
                return _current_page_origin(turn.task_id), method
            with _profile_runtime_scope(home):
                origin, login_method = await asyncio.to_thread(login_origin)
        if not origin or urlsplit(origin).scheme!='https':
            raise AccessError('Open the account\'s HTTPS login page before requesting credentials.')
        host = urlsplit(origin).hostname
        # The hostname is authoritative; an optional account label is display-only.
        label = (label.strip()[:120]+' · '+host) if label.strip() else host+' login'
        if login_method == 'sms' and use_primary:
            from agent.vault_store import VaultStore
            from .personal import PersonalStore
            owner_home = self.private_home(turn.source.scope_id, turn.source.user_id)
            with self.lock_for(owner_home):
                vault = VaultStore(owner_home / 'vault')
                existing = [meta for meta in vault.list_items() if meta.kind == 'login' and meta.login_method == 'sms' and meta.origin == origin]
                primary = PersonalStore(owner_home).values('phone')
                # A website-specific saved number wins over the primary. Multiple
                # accounts require choosing a handle; never silently choose one.
                meta = existing[0] if primary and len(existing) == 1 else None
                if not existing and primary:
                    meta = vault.add_item('login', label, {'login_method': 'sms', 'phone_number': primary['phone_number']}, origin=origin)
                if meta:
                    return {'status': 'access_ready', 'handle': meta.id, 'origin': origin, 'login_method': 'sms',
                            'next': 'Use clanker_vault_fill for this saved login, then request the website SMS and use clanker_vault_enter_code. A fresh SMS code is required.'}
        request = self.store.create(team=turn.source.scope_id,owner=turn.source.user_id,
                                    home=self.private_home(turn.source.scope_id,turn.source.user_id),
                                    task_id=turn.task_id,source=turn.source.to_dict(),task=turn.message,
                                    kind='login',label=label,origin=origin,
                                    identifier=identifier.strip()[:320],login_method=login_method,
                                    gateway_event_id=turn.message_id)
        await self.deliver_link(request)
        return {'status':'waiting_for_owner','request_id':request['id'],'origin':origin,'login_method':login_method,
                'next':'The private secure link has been sent. End this turn with a brief waiting update. Saving access resumes this task automatically.'}

    async def deliver_link(self, row):
        if row.get('message_ts'):
            return
        member = self.validate_member(row['team'],row.get('approver') or row['owner'])
        from uuid import uuid5, NAMESPACE_URL
        message_id = str(uuid5(NAMESPACE_URL,'clanker-access:'+row['id']))
        history = await self.policy.client().conversations_history(channel=member['dm_id'],limit=100)
        posted = next((m for m in history.get('messages',[]) if m.get('client_msg_id')==message_id),None)
        if not posted:
            url = self.config['public_url'].rstrip('/')+'/vault/fill#'+urlencode({'r':row['id'],'token':self.store.token(row['id'])})
            source = json.loads(row['source'])
            instructions={'code':("Enter your current verification code securely. I'll continue after you submit it.",'Enter verification code'),
                          'login':("Add your login securely. I'll continue after you save it.",'Add login to vault'),
                          'api_key':("Add your API key securely. I'll continue after you save it.",'Add API key to vault'),
                          'payment':("Review this purchase and add or approve your card privately. No payment is authorized until you approve the form.",'Review card and purchase')}
            instruction,button=instructions[row['kind']]
            posted = await self.policy.client().chat_postMessage(channel=member['dm_id'],
                thread_ts=(source.get('thread_id') or None) if not row.get('approver') else None,client_msg_id=message_id,unfurl_links=False,unfurl_media=False,
                text=urlsplit(row['origin']).hostname+': '+instruction,
                blocks=[{'type':'section','text':{'type':'plain_text','text':row['label']+'\n'+instruction}},
                        {'type':'actions','elements':[{'type':'button','text':{'type':'plain_text','text':button},'url':url,'action_id':'clanker_vault_link'}]}])
        with self.store.connection() as db:
            db.execute('UPDATE requests SET message_ts=? WHERE id=?', (posted['ts'],row['id']))

    async def request_code(self, turn, meta, *, access=None):
        self.assert_private(turn)
        home=self.private_home(turn.source.scope_id,turn.source.user_id)
        access = access or self.delegations.resolve(turn, meta.id)
        row=self.store.create(team=turn.source.scope_id,owner=turn.source.user_id,home=home,task_id=turn.task_id,
            source=turn.source.to_dict(),task=turn.message,kind='code',label=meta.label+' verification',
            origin=meta.origin,identifier='' if meta.login_method=='sms' else meta.identifier or '',handle=access.handle,
            login_method=meta.login_method,
            grant_id=access.grant_id,approver=access.owner if access.grant_id else None,
            gateway_event_id=turn.message_id)
        await self.deliver_link(row)
        return {'status':'waiting_for_owner','request_id':row['id'],
                'next':'A private secure code form has been sent. End this turn. Submitting the code resumes the task automatically.'}

    def delivery_owned(self, key, event_id):
        """A native final-response obligation owns delivery across the outbox crash gap."""
        from gateway.delivery_ledger import _db_path, compute_obligation_id
        import sqlite3
        path=_db_path()
        if not path.exists():return False
        with sqlite3.connect('file:'+str(path)+'?mode=ro',uri=True) as db:
            if not db.execute("SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='delivery_obligations'").fetchone():return False
            for oid,content in db.execute('SELECT obligation_id,content FROM delivery_obligations WHERE session_key=?',(key,)):
                if oid==compute_obligation_id(key,event_id,content):return True
        return False

    async def resume(self, row, *, transfer=False):
        from gateway.session import SessionSource
        from gateway.platforms.event import MessageEvent
        member = self.validate_member(row['team'],row['owner'])
        source = SessionSource.from_dict(json.loads(row['source']))
        channel_task = self.channel_tasks.restore(source)
        finish=self.store.mark_transfer_resumed if transfer else self.store.mark_resumed
        if channel_task:
            if channel_task['task_state'] in ('completed','result_pending','cancelled'):
                finish(row['id'])
                return
            await self.channel_tasks.validate_destination(channel_task)
            await self.policy.serve_profile(source.profile)
            self.channel_tasks.execution_route(source)
        if not transfer:
            self.delegations.request_access(row)
        expected_profile = source.profile if channel_task else member['profile']
        if source.chat_id!=member['dm_id'] or source.profile!=expected_profile or self.private_home(row['team'],row['owner'])!=Path(row['home']):
            raise AccessError('The original private task is no longer authorized.',403)
        if not self.store.is_pending(row['id'],transfer=transfer):return
        prefix=(("Continue the original channel task using only this requester's authorized account. "
                 "This is an isolated task: do not use unrelated private conversations or files. "
                 "The backend returns your final requested result to the original channel thread. "
                 "Login and code forms are delivered privately. Do not include credentials or access links in the result."
                 if channel_task else "Continue the requester's private account task. Keep account observations and results in this DM.") if transfer else
                f"{'Verification code submitted; use clanker_vault_enter_code' if row['kind']=='code' else 'Access saved'} for {row['label']} ({row['origin']}). Credential handle: {row['handle']}. Continue the original task below, verifying the result before reporting completion.")
        if not transfer and row['kind']=='payment':
            prefix=f"The owner approved purchase request {row['id']}. Use clanker_pay with this request_id in the existing local checkout. This approval is single use and expires quickly. Verify the merchant receipt before reporting paid; never automatically retry an unknown outcome."
        event_id=('clanker-private-resume-' if transfer else 'clanker-access-resume-')+row['id']
        event = MessageEvent(source=source,user_id=source.user_id,user_name=source.user_name,
            text=prefix+'\n\nOriginal request: '+row['task'],message_id=event_id,
            allow_gateway_control=False,metadata={'clanker_private_resume' if transfer else 'clanker_access_resume':row['id']})
        # Use the native gateway turn/delivery path and await its completion. The
        # saved record stays retryable across shutdown, with no secret in events.
        adapter = self.policy.adapter
        adapter._canonicalize(source)
        key = adapter._event_session_key(event)
        if key in adapter._active_sessions:
            return
        if channel_task:
            if self.store.channel_task_requested_access(source.to_dict(),event_id):
                # This native turn durably handed off to a form. Its saved
                # request owns continuation even if the waiting reply was not
                # acknowledged before shutdown, or the form is already saved.
                finish(row['id'])
                return
            recovered = await asyncio.to_thread(self.channel_tasks.recover_response,channel_task,event_id)
            if recovered is not None:
                await self.channel_tasks.handle_response(event,recovered,getattr(adapter,'gateway_runner',None))

import asyncio

}


def verify_slack_token(token, key, audience, nonce):
    try:
        claims = jwt.decode(token,key,algorithms=['RS256'],audience=audience,
                            issuer='https://slack.com',options={'require':['exp','iat','iss','aud','nonce','sub']})
        if not hmac.compare_digest(str(claims['nonce']),nonce):
            raise ValueError('nonce')
        identity={'team':claims['https://slack.com/team_id'],'owner':claims['https://slack.com/user_id']}
        if not all(isinstance(value,str) and value for value in identity.values()):
            raise ValueError('identity')
        return identity
    except (jwt.PyJWTError,ValueError,KeyError):
        raise AccessError('Slack sign-in could not be verified.',403) from None


class VaultWeb:
    def __init__(self, service, config, *, verify_identity=None):
        self.service, self.store, self.config = service, service.store, config
        self.origin = config['public_url'].rstrip('/')
        parts = urlsplit(self.origin)
        if parts.scheme != 'https' and not config.get('local_test'):
            raise ValueError('The hosted credential form requires HTTPS')
        if parts.path not in ('','/') or parts.query or parts.fragment or parts.username or not parts.hostname:
            raise ValueError('public_url must be a website origin')
        self.verify_identity = verify_identity or self.slack_identity
        self.app = web.Application(client_max_size=16384, middlewares=[self.errors])
        self.app.router.add_get('/vault/fill',self.page)
        self.app.router.add_get('/vault',self.page)
        self.app.router.add_get('/assets/vault.js',self.asset)
        self.app.router.add_get('/assets/vault.css',self.asset)
        self.app.router.add_get('/auth/callback',self.callback)
        self.app.router.add_get('/health',self.health)
        self.app.router.add_post('/auth/start',self.auth_start)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/request',self.request)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/save',self.save)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/api-key',self.api_key)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/payment',self.payment)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/payment/decline',self.decline_payment)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/code',self.code)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/items',self.items)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/personal/details',self.personal_details)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/personal/save',self.personal_save)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/personal/remove',self.personal_remove)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/disconnect',self.disconnect)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/invitations',self.invitations)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/invite',self.invite)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/invite/revoke',self.revoke_invitation)

    @web.middleware
    async def errors(self, request, handler):
        try:
            if request.method=='POST' and request.headers.get('Origin')!=self.origin:
                raise AccessError('This request did not come from the credential form.', 403)
            response = await handler(request)
        except AccessError as exc:
            response = web.json_response({'error':str(exc)},status=exc.status)
        except (ValueError,KeyError,TypeError,json.JSONDecodeError):
            response = web.json_response({'error':'The request is invalid.'},status=400)
        except web.HTTPException as exc:
            response = web.Response(body=exc.body,status=exc.status,headers=exc.headers)
        except Exception:
            # Never echo exception bodies: a vault/provider exception may contain input.
            response = web.json_response({'error':'Could not complete this operation. Your task is still saved.'},status=503)
        response.headers.update(SECURITY_HEADERS)
        if not self.config.get('local_test'):
            response.headers['Strict-Transport-Security']='max-age=31536000'
        return response

    async def health(self, request):
        return web.json_response({'ready':True})

    async def page(self, request):
        return web.Response(text=Path(__file__).with_name('page.html').read_text(),content_type='text/html')

    async def asset(self, request):
        name = request.path.rsplit('/',1)[-1]
        return web.Response(text=Path(__file__).with_name(name).read_text(),content_type='text/javascript' if name.endswith('.js') else 'text/css')

    def identity(self, request, *, csrf=False):
        identity = self.store.session(request.cookies.get('__Host-clanker',''))
        self.service.validate_member(identity['team'],identity['owner'])
        if csrf and not hmac.compare_digest(request.headers.get('X-CSRF-Token',''),identity['csrf']):
            raise AccessError('The form session could not be verified. Reload the page.',403)
        return identity

    async def auth_start(self, request):
        data = await request.json()
        row = self.store.get(data['id'],data['token']) if data else None
        if row:self.service.validate_member(row['team'],row['owner'])
        state,browser,nonce = self.store.start_auth(row['id'] if row else '')
        query = urlencode({'response_type':'code','scope':'openid profile','client_id':self.config['client_id'],
                           'state':state,'nonce':nonce,'team':row['team'] if row else self.service.policy.team,
                           'redirect_uri':self.origin+'/auth/callback'})
        response = web.json_response({'url':'https://slack.com/openid/connect/authorize?'+query})
        response.set_cookie('__Host-clanker-auth',browser,secure=True,httponly=True,samesite='Lax',max_age=600,path='/')
        return response

    async def slack_identity(self, code, nonce):
        from agent.secret_scope import build_profile_secret_scope
        secret = build_profile_secret_scope(self.service.policy.home).get('CLANKER_SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET')
        if not secret:
            raise AccessError('Slack sign-in has not been configured.',503)
        async with ClientSession(timeout=ClientTimeout(total=15)) as client:
            async with client.post('https://slack.com/api/openid.connect.token',data={
                'client_id':self.config['client_id'],'client_secret':secret,'code':code,
                'redirect_uri':self.origin+'/auth/callback'}) as response:
                result = await response.json()
        if not result.get('ok') or not result.get('id_token'):
            raise AccessError('Slack could not verify this sign-in. Open your access link again.',403)
        def decode():
            key = jwt.PyJWKClient('https://slack.com/openid/connect/keys',timeout=10).get_signing_key_from_jwt(result['id_token'])
            return verify_slack_token(result['id_token'],key.key,self.config['client_id'],nonce)
        return await asyncio.to_thread(decode)

    async def callback(self, request):
        auth = self.store.consume_auth(request.query.get('state',''),request.cookies.get('__Host-clanker-auth',''))
        identity = await self.verify_identity(request.query.get('code',''),auth['nonce'])
        if auth['request_id']:self.store.get(auth['request_id'],self.store.token(auth['request_id']),identity=identity)
        self.service.validate_member(identity['team'],identity['owner'])
        sid = self.store.new_session(identity['team'],identity['owner'])
        response = web.Response(status=302,headers={'Location':'/vault/fill' if auth['request_id'] else '/vault'})
        response.set_cookie('__Host-clanker',sid,secure=True,httponly=True,samesite='Lax',max_age=3600,path='/')
        response.del_cookie('__Host-clanker-auth',path='/')
        return response

    async def request(self, request):

        row = self.store.get(data['id'],data['token'],identity=self.identity(request))

        if row['kind'] in ('login', 'code'):result['login_method']=row['login_method']

            result['defaults']={}
            email=personal.values('email')
            phone=personal.values('phone')
            if email and not row['identifier']:result['defaults']['email']=email['email']
            if phone and row['login_method']=='sms':result['defaults']['phone_number']=phone['phone_number']
        if row['kind']=='payment':result['payment']=await asyncio.to_thread(self.service.payments.view,row)
        return web.json_response(result)

        identity=self.identity(request,csrf=True);data=await request.json()
        label=await asyncio.to_thread(self.service.approve_payment,data['id'],data['token'],identity,data['fields'])

    async def decline_payment(self, request):

        self.service.private_home(identity['team'],identity['owner'])
        await asyncio.to_thread(self.service.payments.decline,data['id'],data['token'],identity)

        identity = self.identity(request,csrf=True)

        return 'https://slack.com/app_redirect?'+urlencode({'team':identity['team'],'channel':member['dm_id']})

    async def api_key(self, request):
        identity=self.identity(request,csrf=True)
        data=await request.json()
        return_url=self.return_slack_url(identity)
        meta=await asyncio.to_thread(self.service.save_api_key,data['id'],data['token'],identity,data['fields'])
        return web.json_response({'saved':True,'label':meta.label,'return_slack_url':return_url})

    async def items(self, request):
